#2083. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Old Trafford and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#2082. Exclusive: Fresh Robbie Fowler to Swindon Town update revealed after Ian Holloway sack

Swindon Town are on the search for a new manager, with Ian Holloway's time at the County Ground coming to an end earlier in the week.

The 63-year-old had been in charge of the Robins for the past two years, having endured a storied career which has taken him to the Premier League with both Blackpool and Crystal Palace.

Improvement was showed in both seasons finished by Holloway, with 12th and ninth-placed finishes in League Two, but results have been indifferent during the current campaign, with back-to-back defeats over Grimsby Town and Newport County leading to his dismissal.

Swindon's hierarchy - which includes chairman Clem Morfuni - must now find Holloway's successor, and FLW can exclusively reveal that one individual who is on the radar is none other than Premier League legend Robbie Fowler.

Fowler scored 163 Premier League goals in his career for Liverpool, Leeds United and Manchester City, whilst also appearing 26 times for the England national team, before winding down his career in Australia and Thailand.

We looked at five potential replacements Swindon Town should consider if they part company with under-pressure manager Ian Holloway.

Since his retirement, Fowler has been well-travelled as a manager, with spells in both Thailand and Australia, as well as India and Saudi Arabia, but he's yet to land a job in his native England, having been without a role since being with Al-Qadsiah in 2023.

That could now change though, with Football League World understanding that the 51-year-old is a live contender to become the latest person to have a go at the Town job.

One of the reasons that Fowler is being admired by Swindon chairman Morfuni is his time in his native Australia, FLW can reveal.

After a spell at Blackburn Rovers, Fowler moved down under in 2009 to play for North Queensland Fury, a stint which lasted a year before moving on to fellow Aussie club Perth Glory.

Fowler would join Muangthong United in Thailand in 2011 and end up becoming their player-manager for a short period of time, but some eight years after leaving Australia, the former striker would return as a manager, taking the Brisbane Roar job.

Managing 23 games for the Queensland-based outfit, Fowler won 11 times as their manager, before the A-League was suspended in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic - he wouldn't return to the club as he relocated to be closer to his family.

A further 20 matches were managed for East Bengal between 2020 and 2021, before a stint in Saudi with Al-Qadsiah lasted just three months, despite winning six of his eight matches in charge and going unbeaten in the Saudi second tier, with the club wanting to move to a more Spanish-style model, according to Fowler himself.

#2081. Dave Challinor sends Sheffield Wednesday message after Barry Bannan captaincy query

Sheffield Wednesday's captaincy situation has been played down by Dave Challinor, despite Barry Bannan handing the armband to Liam Cooper and not Liam Palmer in last Friday night's win at Barnsley.

Henrik Pedersen installed Palmer as the club captain in January when Bannan left Hillsborough to join Millwall. After returning to Sheffield Wednesday in the summer, Bannan didn't pick up the armband he left behind, with Palmer instead continuing in the role.

However, the defender has been in just three starting line-ups this season, meaning Bannan has taken over the armband a considerable amount of the time under both Pedersen and Challinor.

In last Friday's win against Barnsley at Oakwell, Bannan wore the armband until he was replaced by Harry Gray in the 78th minute. Despite Palmer coming off the bench seven minutes earlier, it was Cooper who took the armband.

In the wake of that happening, Challinor was quizzed by Joe Crann of The Wednesday Word about the captaincy situation.

He responded by confirming he'd not given who wore the armband at Oakwell much thought at all.

"I've given it zero thought," he said. "Baz came off and whoever he passes the armband to (is the captain). I've said before, I'm not huge on — I know some of them (the players and fans) will be — who wears the armband."

Challinor also offered an insight into his leadership group: "We have a group that I spoke to on the first day I came into the building — the leadership group. Baz, Palms (Palmer), Coops (Cooper), Lummers (Joe Lumley), Billy (Mitchell) and Dish (Di-Shon Bernard) are all part of that. It makes no odds, I want leaders on the pitch.

"If you're wearing an armband, it makes no difference to me."

Wednesday are back in action on Saturday afternoon when they host Reading FC at Hillsborough.

Who should be Sheffield Wednesday captain? Let us know in the comments!

Pedersen was in a difficult position when Bannan walked out of Hillsborough to go to Millwall, and the obvious choice was to give the captaincy to Palmer — a long-standing member of the squad and someone who had stuck with Wednesday through difficult periods.

Bannan's return to the club in the summer led to many believing he would take on the captaincy again, but Pedersen rightly stuck by the man who had stuck by Wednesday in Palmer.

The fact Palmer isn't a guaranteed starter makes this a topic of discussion once again. If Bannan is starting the majority of games and Palmer isn't, he will naturally wear the armband more. The same can be said of Cooper, who has started 13 times in the league this season. He was the club captain at Leeds United for a decade and led them to the Premier League — he's another strong candidate to captain Wednesday.

A new manager also brings new ideas, and Challinor won't have the loyalty to Palmer that Pedersen did. He's also clearly got a few contenders in Lumley, Mitchell and Bernard, who could be longer-term options for the captaincy.

A change in the coming months would be no surprise.

#2080. West Ham must muscle in on Celtic transfer target to solve major Scott Parker headache

West Ham have had a very poor season so far in the Championship, with the Hammers way off the pace for a top two finish.

Not only did many observers expect the Hammers to bounce back to the Premier League at the first attempt, but they were widely tipped to win the league.

Therefore, the fact they are in the bottom half after 17 games, and some 11 points away from second-place is a massive underachievement.

Nuno Espírito Santo paid the price for an inconsistent start by losing his job at the start of the month, but the decision to appoint Scott Parker hasn’t paid off just yet, as the former player is without a win in four.

However, with Parker having won promotion from the Championship with three different clubs, there’s no doubting his CV at this level. So, his early struggles have opened up a wider discussion on why West Ham are failing, and the players are coming under scrutiny.

In truth, you could identify several areas of the pitch that need addressing, but there’s no doubt that the goalkeeper position is giving Parker a major headache at the moment.

Mads Hermansen started as his number one, but the Dane has had a terrible time of things since he moved to the Londoners, and he was taken out of the firing line after a poor performance at Blackburn a few weeks ago.

With Alphonse Areola injured, youngster Fin Herrick has had the gloves for the past two games, but he didn’t convince for Preston’s opener last Saturday, and he made a mistake in the 1-0 defeat to Portsmouth on Tuesday.

So, it remains to be seen who starts against Stoke, with Areola likely to play if he is available. Yet, even if he is, the Frenchman hasn’t exactly played well for West Ham for a long time now, and there are doubts over both his fitness and mentality.

Therefore, bringing in a new number one could quickly become a priority for Parker as soon as the window opens in January, and Blackburn’s Balazs Toth is someone who should be on their radar.

The Hungarian was heavily linked with Celtic in the summer transfer window, but Rovers managed to keep him at Ewood Park, although he's still thought to be a target for the Glasgow giants.

Toth has shown why he was so highly regarded after producing some big saves for Blackburn this season, although he perhaps hasn’t got back to the heights he had set in the previous campaign.

Unfortunately for Blackburn and Toth, he is currently out with a hand injury sufered on international duty with Hungary that could sideline him until mid-January, but he has done enough over the years to earn a reputation as a reliable Championship keeper.

Due to his injury, it’s no exaggeration to say there’s a possibility that Toth has played his last game for Blackburn, as there are major doubts over his future going into the New Year.

That’s because Toth’s contract is expiring in the summer of 2027, so, unless fresh terms are agreed, then this will be the last window for Rovers to get a fee for the 29-year-old.

It has been claimed previously that Toth is not keen on signing an extension, so that will put clubs on alert going into January.

Whether Blackburn are willing to sanction a sale when they have a chance to make the play-offs remains to be seen, but it would certainly make financial sense to avoid letting an asset go for nothing.

From West Ham’s perspective, Toth’s contract means he is a very realistic target in what could be a challenging month for the club.

If West Ham remain off the pace in terms of pushing for the top two, selling clubs will know that the Irons are desperate.

#2078. Lincoln City warned against repeating Michael Skubala 'experiment' with Gavin Strachan

Lincoln City are on the hunt for a new head coach after parting company with Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw earlier this week.

Lincoln won the League One title last season to secure a return to the second tier of English football for the first time in 65 years, but just weeks after sealing promotion, they lost head coach Michael Skubala to Bristol City, with Cohen and Shaw stepping up to replace him.

It is fair to say that Lincoln's decision to appoint Cohen and Shaw as joint-head coaches raised a few eyebrows, and they were widely tipped for relegation at the start of the season, but the pair made an impressive start to life in the Sincil Bank dugout.

After losing their opening two games, the Imps went on a five-game unbeaten run which lifted them to as high as eighth in the Championship table in mid-September, but results have declined significantly in recent months.

Lincoln have won just one of their last 10 games, and after suffering their fifth consecutive defeat as they were hammered 4-0 at Charlton Athletic on Tuesday night, Cohen and Shaw were dismissed on Wednesday morning with the club sitting 21st, just three points clear of the relegation zone.

There has been a shortage of rumours about potential successors to Cohen and Shaw so far, but journalist Alan Nixon reported on Thursday that West Bromwich Albion coach Gavin Strachan is one name under consideration by the Imps.

Strachan has plenty of coaching experience under his belt, having previously worked at the likes of Peterborough United, Doncaster Rovers and Celtic, and he has been part of James Morrison's backroom staff at The Hawthorns since the summer, but his only managerial experience is a brief four-and-a-half month spell with seventh tier side Ilkeston in 2015.

When asked for his thoughts on the possible appointment of Strachan, FLW's Lincoln City fan pundit Gary Hutchinson insisted that the Imps cannot afford to take a risk like they did with Skubala in League One, and he urged the club to bring in a manager with Championship experience.

"I think Gavin Strachan would be too much of a gamble for the club," Gary told FLW.

"I think they're looking for somebody with managerial experience.

"We're not in the same position as when we appointed Michael Skubala.

"When we were in League One, even though we were a smaller fish, there were always six or seven teams below us with smaller budgets, so we were expected not to be in the bottom four.

"The bottom four was failure, so we could afford to experiment a little bit, and that was the case with Michael Skubala.

"I think this calls for the same sort of thing as we had in the National League, get a manager in who understands the division a little bit more and who perhaps has experience of handling players and picking players up because they're going to need that.

"That performance on Tuesday night was not good enough.

"Whilst Gavin Strachan may well be a very good coach, we've had two coaches at the helm, and I think we need somebody who's got experience of the top job, as well as the coaching credentials.

"Bear in mind, on the coaching field, we've got Paul McShane and Shaun Pearson, who are both very competent coaches, so we need a figurehead to pull that back in.

"I just think, with Gavin Strachan, his lack of actual managerial experience will hold him back."

Who has the best and worst average attendances in the Championship so far this season? Football League World takes a look...

Lincoln have often taken gambles with their managerial decisions over the years, and they were certainly rewarded for the bold appointment of Skubala, whose only senior dugout experience prior to his arrival at Sincil Bank was a few games as caretaker of Leeds United in the Premier League.

However, the failed Cohen and Shaw experiment underlines the dangers of such risks in the Championship, and while the duo's time in charge should not be remembered as a disaster given that the Imps are currently outside the relegation zone, they should learn lessons and make a safer choice on this occasion.

Who should Lincoln City target to replace Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw? Tell us in the comments below!

Strachan is clearly a talented coach who has enjoyed plenty of success during his career, including helping Celtic to five consecutive Scottish Premiership titles, and he has made a big impact at West Brom this season, but he would not be the right man for Lincoln at this time.

#2076. Top 20 most valuable EFL League One strikers right now

Strikers are where the big money lies, and every club across the EFL wants their line-leaders to have high value.

In League One, that's no different, and with the third tier looking the tightest it's been in quite some time this season, a good number nine could end up being the difference between staying up or going down, mid-table or the play-offs, or maybe even going up automatically.

We saw last season how Leyton Orient's third-tier status was heavily preserved by Dom Ballard's goals and how the excellence of Bim Pepple and Lorent Tolaj drove a once hapless Plymouth Argyle side up the division in the second half of the season.

Two of those went for big money to Bristol City this past summer, but which current League One strikers could do the same?

According to Transfermarkt's data, these are the 20 strikers with the most value in the third tier right now.

N.B. All values are initially in Euros - converted to Pounds for the list

MK Dons re-signed Sam Nombe this past summer from Rotherham United for a guaranteed £600,000, which could surpass £1 million if add-ons are met.

The 28-year-old was bought when the Millers were in the Championship off the back of a 15-goal season with Exeter City, and then would score 14 and 12 in the last two seasons at the level in South Yorkshire, albeit last year ending in relegation.

That would have dropped his value, per Tranfsermarkt's ranks, but you'd expect another 10-goal season at least in this free-scoring MK side.

It's been a difficult few years for Gassan Ahadme. His value would have been sky-high after being signed for Charlton Athletic off the back of 11 goals in 29 third tier games for Cambridge United in 2023/24.

But, a couple of dud years, whether that be at the Valley in their promotion campaign, or last season at Stevenage, have lowered that back down, and now he's back at the Abbey, already with more league goals than he's managed in his last two seasons combined.

Bosnian frontman Admir Bristric was an intriguing signing for Leicester City to make this past summer. The 23-year-old scored 15 in 29 in all competitions last season for Slovenian side NK Bravo, and the Foxes paid at least €1.15m (£963k) for his services.

Unfortunately, Emil Riis signed less than a month later, and all of a sudden, Bristric was relegated to cameo roles and was quickly shunned out of League One plans.

His only appearances in the last three months have been in the EFL Trophy and the FA Cup against National League North side Oxford City. Even then, he only played three minutes off the bench against the sixth tier side.

Bristric is taking time getting used to the EFL, but if he remains out of Russell Martin's plans, his value will only decrease.

It's very impressive that Tom Bloxham, at only 23 years old, has 200 EFL appearances, most of which have come in League One. He's been, at worst, a useful squad player for around five years now, at Shrewsbury Town, Morecambe or now at Blackpool.

The towering six-foot-five frontman hasn't properly exploded into a 15-to-20-goal striker just yet in his career, but his duarability and potential contribute to Transfermarkt's value.

Perhaps the new Blackpool boss, once they're in the building, can start to get the best out of him.

Age does, unfortunately, have to play a factor in these values, as if Kyle Wootton was six years younger, he'd easily be worth double. He'd also probably be in the Championship, too.

Instead, the 30-year-old has to settle for being one of the best goalscoring big men in the third tier at Stockport County. He finished second in the Golden Boot ranks last season, but it's arguable that he'd have overtaken Dom Ballard if not for an injury crisis which meant he had to play centre-back for the final month of the campaign.

He's already in double digits this season, and is one of the key reasons why Stockport are so good under Jimmy McNulty, as his aerial threat means that they can go long to him if their patient build-up isn't working. Very valuable to the Hatters, but underrepresented on this list.

A position purely based on potential, Leeds United must be really disappointed that their 18-year-old starlet Harry Gray isn't currently excelling on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, and hasn't yet started a game under new boss Dave Challinor, as of writing.

The England Under-19 international is highly-rated both at Leeds and amongst general footballing circles, with him the latest line of Gray's, who are legendary at Elland Road.

The fact he was loaned out aged just 17 to Rotherham in January, instead of playing more youth football, just shows how developed he already is, and once Gray can finally get clicking at the top end of the pitch, his value will only climb higher.

Welsh international Mark Harris couldn't properly get going at Championship level with Oxford United following his 19-goal campaign in all competitions in 2023/24 to help the Yellows get promoted.

Now he's back in League One, though, his golscoring knack has returned. He's already netted more times than he has in each of his two seasons in the second-tier in the first few months of this term.

Transfermarkt's list shows a green arrow next to his £628k value, too, so it's increased since the start of the season.

Bojan Radulovic's value has definitely increased over the past 12 months or so. His Huddersfield Town career seemed to be over back in January 2025, when he was loaned out to Eredivisie side Fortuna Sittard after playing just 855 minutes of League One action.

He found form back at the Accu Stadium under Lee Grant, though, and netted seven in 15 appearances in the first half of last season. Unfortunately, in 2026, he's had an injury-ravaged year.

Radulovic missed lengthy periods towards the back end of last season, and this year has been in and out of the side under Martin Drury. Nevertheless, he still has a handful of league goals in limited minutes, and a full return would make an already threatening Terriers attack even better.

Someone else whose value has skyrocketed in recent times is Aaron Collins. Plainly put, not many were expecting him to have the year he's currently having based on last season's performances in League Two.

FLW has debated which 15 fanbases generate the best atmospheres and more inside their home stadiums

The 29-year-old was one of the big-money MK Dons captures while they were in League Two, having netted at least 10 in three consecutive third tier seasons, but he only scored six league goals last year.

This season, though, he's scoring a goal a game in all competitions, leading the scoring charts in league action, and was awarded his Wales debut against Portugal in the latest round of Nations League games. Arguably, he could, and should, be even higher.

Jacob Brown was signed by Luton Town back in the summer of 2023 in their first campaign as a Premier League club. He'd netted Championship goals for Stoke City across the previous two seasons.

He's kind of lost his way since, like the Hatters have as a football club, in fairness, and after spending last season on loan up a level in the Championship with Portsmouth, he joined Reading on a free transfer at the end of his contract.

It's been a smart bit of business so far for Reading, with Brown one of, if not the best backup strikers in the division. Almost all of his appearances have been off the bench with Jack Marriott ahead of him, and he's still scored four times in league action as of writing.

#2075. PSG transfer news: Spanish winger fits profile to cover Doue and Kvaratskhelia

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 06:57

Paris Saint-Germain may have to turn to the transfer market to deal with a problem that threatens to change Luis Enrique's plans for the rest of the season.

The injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue have left the manager without two of his main options on the flanks of the attack. In that scenario, Athletic Bilbao's Nico Williams appears among the names being monitored by the French club, according to Le Parisien.

At 24, the Spaniard combines speed, dribbling and the ability to play on both sides of the pitch. More than a replacement for the injured pair, he could offer Luis Enrique a characteristic that has become important to the team's attacking play: the ability to unbalance defences without depending on collective combinations.

The importance of Kvaratskhelia and Doue to PSG is not limited to attacking output. Both offer mobility, the ability to carry the ball and the freedom to switch positions during matches. Their simultaneous absence forces Luis Enrique to find alternatives to maintain the unpredictability of a system based on constant movement.

Williams could help in that respect. His main characteristic is the ability to receive the ball wide and run at the full-back. His acceleration allows him to gain an advantage in a few metres. He also stands out for carrying the ball at speed and attacking both the outside channel and the space between full-back and centre-back.

That characteristic fits PSG's structure. Luis Enrique works with a team of fluid positions that nevertheless maintains reference points for occupying the pitch. When Kvaratskhelia moves from the left to occupy inside spaces, Nuno Mendes can advance and take over the width. The movement creates doubts for the opposition defence and allows the Georgian to take part more in build-up play from inside.

Williams could perform a similar dynamic, but with one difference: he tends to stay wider to receive the ball and exploit one-on-one duels. That would not be a problem, as it would give PSG an alternative for situations in which the opponent closes the central spaces and forces the team to find solutions down the flanks.

With the Spaniard wide, Nuno Mendes could better choose when to advance on the outside or take up inside positions. The presence of a winger capable of beating his marker without help would also open up space for runs from Vitinha, Joao Neves and the players who occupy the central area.

Williams also offers an important quality in the final third: he can cross after beating the full-back, but also cut inside and find team-mates in the box. He is not just a sprinter who takes the ball to the byline. His ability to create for others was one of the hallmarks of Athletic's 2024 Copa del Rey campaign and of Spain's Euro 2024 campaign.

Signing Williams would not solve all of PSG's absences, because the three attackers have different characteristics. Kvaratskhelia is especially strong at carrying the ball in tight spaces and creating play from inside. Doue is more versatile, able to play on both sides and also in the middle, combining dribbling, physicality and creativity.

Williams is more vertical. He likes to receive the ball with space to accelerate and to turn seemingly controlled situations into individual duels. Rather than trying to reproduce exactly Kvaratskhelia's movements, he could offer a different way of attacking the same space.

One of PSG's strengths lies in how the team changes its way of attacking depending on the opponent. With Williams, Paris could make more use of depth and duels down the flanks, especially against defences that push their lines up to press the French side's build-up.

The Spaniard could also play on the right, although the left is his most natural position. That versatility would allow him to alternate sides with Mika Godts, as well as offering more possibilities for attacking rotations. There would be no need to tie Williams to a single flank.

There is, however, one point to consider: Williams can still improve his decision-making and finishing efficiency. His game is heavily based on dribbling and acceleration, and the individual move does not always end in the best choice. At PSG, he would have to learn to balance personal initiative with the quick combinations that characterise Luis Enrique's model.

If the tactical fit seems promising, the negotiation is more complicated. Williams renewed with Athletic in July 2025 until 2035, a move that ended, at least at that time, speculation over his departure to Barcelona.

The Basque club announced that the release clause had increased by more than 50 per cent compared with the previous contract. The Spanish press puts the figure at close to £76.5m (€90m).

The length of the contract gives Athletic enormous bargaining power. The club has no need to sell its main attacker and knows that PSG are looking for a solution to a problem created by injuries. If the French side really want the player, they will have to consider paying the clause in full or finding a deal that convinces the Basques.

The player's own wishes also matter. Williams has publicly shown his attachment to Athletic and said, on renewing, that he was where he wanted to be. A move to Paris could represent a sporting and financial leap, but his departure cannot be treated as automatic.

PSG, on the other hand, need to weigh up the length of the problem. The injuries to Doue and Kvaratskhelia are serious and should keep them out for much of the season, but the club does not necessarily need to sign two permanent replacements. The Le Parisien report stresses that the hierarchy has not yet decided whether it will go to the market and is also considering internal alternatives such as Senny Mayulu, Godts and Ferran Torres.

Williams would be an impact signing, able to solve an immediate need and remain important when the injured players return. But paying close to £76.5m for a player who was not necessarily in the plans before the injuries requires a very strong conviction.

#2074. Chris Wilder urged to make 'controversial' Tom Cannon exit decision at Sheffield United

As the Blades continue their impressive form, hopes of a potential promotion push will be increasing in S2, but one man who may not be enjoying his current situation is striker Tom Cannon.

Cannon joined United from Leicester City in January 2025 for a reported fee of around £10 million, but he has scored just 11 goals in 73 appearances during what has been a frustrating near two-year spell at the club.

The 23-year-old has netted three times in 16 games this season, but just nine of those appearances have come from the start, and on what was just his second start in the past month against the Saints in midweek, he was replaced by Patrick Bamford at half time.

#2072. New EFL rule forces QPR to change home shirt design

QPR will have to change the design of their shirt from next season moving forward due to new EFL regulations that will be in place.

The R’s blue-and-white hooped home shirt is arguably one of the most iconic in the Football League, with a host of legendary players having pulled it on over the years at Loftus Road.

However, QPR are now in a position where they will have to alter the design after an EFL update.

That’s because, as explained by West London Sport, the EFL have introduced a new rule that means a ‘number zone’ needs to be free on every shirt.

Essentially, it means that the number on the back of a shirt and the player's name must be free of any patterns or designs.

Of course, the current shirt prevents that from happening, so QPR’s normal design, where the blue-and-white hoop goes all the way around, will need to be changed.

The decision by the EFL was supported by some in the game, with some commentators particularly pleased as it will make reading names and numbers a lot easier. And, the same applies to matchday officials on the pitch, so there is some understanding of the decision.

It should be said that QPR shirts in the past have had a white patch on the back at times, so this isn’t something unique, although most fans in the modern era are used to the blue-and-white hoops going all the way around.

To their credit, the club have interacted with supporters on what next step they will take.

They add that whilst the players must not wear a shirt with hoops that go all the way around, they can still sell shirts to supporters in that way.

Who has the best and worst average attendances in the Championship so far this season? Football League World takes a look...

So, they have allowed fans to vote on whether the replica shirts next season will have full hoops, or if they want the same design as the players.

It will be interesting to see which vote wins, but there will be frustration among the fans that the club has been put in a position where they have to make changes to their shirt.

This is a new regulation in the EFL, but it’s already in place in the Premier League, so even if QPR do win promotion, they are going to be in the same position.

Again, it’s something that some fans may not like, but you do feel sorry for the club, as they have been left in a position where they need to make changes.

Will QPR win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

It’s good to see that they are getting the fans involved, and the QPR shirt will remain an iconic one even with a change.

Now, all the focus will be on ensuring Julien Stephan’s side are wearing the 2027/28 shirt as a Premier League club, as promotion is a real possibility for the Londoners this season, as they are playing good football under the Frenchman, and they will fancy their chances of a top eight finish as a minimum.

#2069. Too late, FA overturns Leny Yoro’s Liverpool red card in Pochettino’s first game

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

However, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino said.

“Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

“But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

The FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have failed to hit the numbers expected off them after a lackluster campaign so far.

Michael Carrick was relieved off his duties after winning just 1 game in his first 10, while collecting only 8 points. Manchester United arr currently languishing in the relegation spots and Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, has a massive task ahead.

Manchester United have been leaky in defence and haven’t gone a game without conceding a goal this season. Their attacking returns are equally disappointing with United failing to convert chances regularly.

Paul Merson believes Manchester United must strengthen their defence in January but insists their problems extend beyond the backline, with concerns over their midfield and attacking options also needing attention.

The January transfer window could be the first stop for Pochettino for some shopping but the budget given to him as per a previous report by readmanutd isn’t much to make a difference.

Paul Merson believes the club have several areas to improve rather than focusing only on their defence.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Arsenal midfielder made it clear that United need to bring in defensive reinforcements.

“Manchester United will have to get centre-halves in, defenders in and full-backs in,” Merson said.

However, Merson does not believe defensive recruitment alone will solve United’s problems. He also questioned the team’s ability to control games in midfield and expressed concerns about the quality of their attacking options.

“I wouldn’t say that’s just been the problem. I don’t think they’ve got legs in midfield, I don’t think they’re dominating games in midfield,” he explained.

He was also critical of United’s forward line, suggesting that the current attacking options are not consistently performing.

“I’ve never really been a massive fan of their front three. I think they’re not Manchester United standard, in my opinion.”

Merson also compared the current generation with some of the club’s former greats, including Wayne Rooney, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Roy Keane, Paul Scholes, David Beckham and Cristiano Ronaldo. He compared players’ consistency with those earlier.

“Back in the day when it’s Rooney and them kind of players and Van Nistelrooy and Keane and Scholes and Beckham and Ronaldo, they were seven, eight out of ten every week. There wasn’t a four out of ten and a nine out of ten.”

“And if they have a four the week after, it doesn’t really matter. So for me, it hasn’t just been the defence.”

United could face difficult decisions when the transfer window opens, particularly if they want to strengthen multiple areas of the squad and with the budget available to Pochettino, that doesn’t seem to be the case.

#2065. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record as Arsenal teenager makes England history

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

The Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

An early strike from Afonso Moreira gave Portugal the lead in the 28th minute. An ineffective England team failed to respond. However, the replacements gave Lee Carsley’s team some late momentum.

Despite the hosts’ attempts to level the score, they failed to break down the Portuguese defence. The result means England have lost for the second game running. However, Dowman had much to be pleased with personally.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It shows how quickly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a big impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

England will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

#2061. Martin Ødegaard sends clear message to Arsenal amid Bayern Munich transfer rumours

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Martin Ødegaard has spoken out about the speculation surrounding his future. He has stated he would like to stay at Arsenal for the future.

The captain has also admitted that talks about a new deal have not yet begun. Ødegaard is currently under contract until the summer of 2028. This leaves Arsenal with an important decision to make over the coming months.

Bayern Munich are being linked with an interest in the midfielder according to reports from Germany. The Bundesliga giants are said to be keeping their eyes on the player’s situation.

Speaking while on international duty with Norway, Ødegaard was quick to dismiss the speculation. He made it clear he is settled in north London and sees his future being at the Emirates Stadium.

There is no suggestion that the 27-year-old is seeking a move. Although comments do highlight a contract issue that Arsenal will be keen to resolve in the short term.

The Norwegian’s laid-back attitude should be encouraging for supporters.

He has made it clear that he is happy at the club and wants to stay here for the time being. This means that there is no need to panic.

Since his permanent move from Real Madrid in 2021, Ødegaard has become a key player in Mikel Arteta’s plans. He has grown into a team leader and is one of the most influential players in the dressing room.

His importance has been shown by his inclusion in all 10 of Arsenal’s Premier League games so far this season. He has scored three goals.

Arsenal have put themselves in a good position in the title race. Keeping their key players happy will be important in the second half of the campaign.

The Gunners will be focused on their game against Newcastle United on 21st November.

#2060. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

#2058. Arsenal Women held by London City Lionesses despite Frida Maanum goal

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

London City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

The Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

#2057. Malo Gusto’s Kante Lesson Gives Chelsea A £75m Xabi Alonso Decision

Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

That matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the important detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

That is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

The Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive plans, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

One is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

The other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

The complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness issues, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

Palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

This is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

If Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

Manchester United are reportedly leaning towards allowing Lisandro Martinez to leave next summer, with the club increasingly doubtful about extending the defender’s contract beyond the current season.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, Jacobs suggested that Manchester United are already considering a defensive rebuild ahead of next summer.

“I think the Lisandro Martinez direction of travel is a departure, and there is the option to extend by one year. But my gut says that Manchester United, even if they can’t get defenders in the winter, will add further in the summer,” Jacobs said.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Declan Rice’s new contract shows how much of an asset he is to Mikel Arteta. His recent performances show why.

The England international has reportedly signed a new five-year deal which will keep him at the Emirates Stadium until 2031. The contract is a reward for the midfielder who has been instrumental in Arsenal’s success since he moved to the club in 2023 from West Ham.

Rice has not just provided the presence and protection that Arsenal were hoping for with their £105 million signing. He has continued to develop his game, especially after returning to his deeper midfield role this season.

Rice came in as a defensive midfielder, but Arteta quickly saw how much he could offer higher up the park.

His physicality, ability to run into the box and set piece threat made him a useful left-sided number eight. Rice had a huge impact in midfield for Arsenal, bringing goals and a new attacking threat.

But Rice has played in a more advanced position on the right-hand side of the midfield duo this season, and this has not limited his impact but instead highlighted another key part of his game.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

This is of particular interest, as he has often come under criticism for his distribution. But he is averaging nearly double the amount of line-breaking passes he did last season.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a new contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

The reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding new ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.
