#2022. Danny Drinkwater on Chelsea move he ‘could never turn down’

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day plans back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar issue. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s plans after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

Max Dowman shortly returns to action for Arsenal after serving a three-game suspension.

His absence has been disappointing, but the experience should give the youngster an important lesson. Can he put the incident behind him and show Mikel Arteta that he can be trusted?

Dowman received a red card against Fleetwood Town after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Arsenal appealed the decision, but the FA rejected the club’s appeal.

The suspension ruled him out of three domestic fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle United.

He’ll be back on 29 November as Arsenal take on Manchester City. This should give the young star a chance to get his season back on track and showcase what makes him such a highly-rated player.

Dowman looks very promising for the future. He has shown great adaptability playing with the more experienced players and has the self-belief to make an impact in games.

He has performed well in the Carabao Cup. In the 4-2 win against Ipswich, Dowman scored two goals, showing his flair and poise in front of goal.

Arteta has given him opportunities to play in the Premier League and Champions League, meaning that he appears to have a clear route into the first team.

Although Dowman still has a lot to learn, he displays great potential in his technical ability and combative nature. As he gets more games under his belt, fans will be excited to see how he progresses.

Dowman was sent off in an unfortunate moment. He was heavily challenged by Neal and, after lashing out, was shown a straight red card.

Although this one moment should not be enough to dismiss a young player from the game completely, it can serve as a valuable lesson on the pressure that comes with playing at a higher level.

Opponents will test Dowman physically, but he must learn to keep his composure. As he starts making an impact, some players may target his age and inexperience to unsettle him.

As he gets more game time, consistency will be key. Arteta must be confident that Dowman can be relied on in high pressure situations.

Arsenal do not need to rush Dowman into the first team. The squad’s quality allows Arteta to manage his minutes and give him time to develop without putting too much pressure on him.

If Dowman is to play against Manchester City, it will depend on Arteta’s plans, but he has certainly done enough to warrant consideration.

The suspension should not define his season. What matters now is how he responds, both on and off the pitch.

Dowman has the talent to become an important player for Arsenal. Keeping his discipline will be just as important as displaying his ability.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend with a growing treatment table and a lot of questions for Xabi Alonso to answer before Saturday’s visit of Bournemouth.

The main concern revolves around Joao Pedro. Chelsea’s current player of the season rescued a point against newly promoted Hull, but he suffered a knock and sat out the damaging 3-0 defeat at Brentford. The problem also prompted his removal from Brazil’s squad shortly after he had returned to it.

Moises Caicedo has also struggled with an injury this season, playing just 14 minutes across the campaign. He’s spent the majority of time on the bench recovering from a bad calf injury, which ruled him out for most of the season.

Captain Reece James missed the Brentford game with yet another hamstring problem. Alonso said he only just missed out, so a return seems likely.

There may also be debuts. Marco Palestra, the £27m signing from Atalanta, has been sidelined since a training injury just before the opening match against Fulham. He is back in full training and was expected to feature in a behind-closed-doors friendly with Portsmouth. Chelsea lost 2-0. Emmanuel Emegha, injured after scoring against Bromley in July, is also pushing for involvement.

Less clear is the position of Jamie Gittens. He limped off with an ankle injury playing for England Under-21s against Kazakhstan and was seen on crutches. Mike Penders is fine after a quad scare on Belgium duty. Returning to the bench against Turkey.

Chelsea badly need a lift. Defeat at Brentford before the break left Alonso’s side looking shaky, and a squad stretched by injuries has not helped.

Saturday brings a chance to steady things. If Palmer, James and Caicedo are available, with Palestra and Emegha potentially adding fresh options, the picture will look much brighter at Stamford Bridge. Joao Pedro’s absence will still sting. However, a strong response against Bournemouth would go a long way towards easing the pressure and restoring belief.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their attacking options in January. One player they are reportedly keeping an eye on is Brentford winger Kevin Schade. Mikel Arteta will be keen to add competition in attack, and Schade may be a good option.

Schade will give additional pace to the offence. He is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions to provide Arteta with extra depth in the squad.

However, it may be difficult to get Schade. He is on loan at Brentford, and may want to keep him in the long term. If Schade is seen as a key player in the future, they may be difficult to negotiate with.

Schade’s versatility is another big plus. His speed and straightforward method make him hard to deal with for defenders. In addition, he can be used as a left-sided attacker, giving Arteta more flexibility in his front line. As the club are playing in a number of competitions, this can be very useful.

Schade has already scored 3 times in the Premier League this season. He has quickly adapted to playing in England after moving from Freiburg to Brentford in 2023.

Despite only being 24 years old, Schade still has a lot to improve on. He has lots of experience in the Premier League but has not quite reached the peak of his ability yet. If he moves to Arsenal, he may be able to elevate his performance.

Brentford has already started negotiations with Schade regarding a contract extension that would keep him tied to the club for a long time. He is already contracted until the summer of 2028.

Arsenal’s interest in Schade is logical. His versatility will provide Arteta with additional flexibility because of his prior experience in the Premier League.

It can be considered positive to sign new strikers. Arsenal must decide if they believe that Schade will fit in well with their current players and whether the asking price from Brentford is reasonable.

As of now, there are no signs of a transfer on the horizon, but it is clear that Schade is a player worth monitoring as the winter transfer window approaches.

#2016. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

#2014. Pep Guardiola names three former midfielders he expects to become good managers, including an ex-Man City player

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 09:15

Pep Guardiola believes that midfielders have characteristics that can make the transition from the pitch to the technical area easier.

In an interview with Romario TV, the former Manchester City manager spoke about players who, in his view, have the potential to build a successful career as managers, and highlighted the broader vision of the game that the position requires.

Among the names mentioned are Ilkay Gundogan, Sergio Busquets and Xabi Alonso, all with midfield experience and different trajectories in football. When asked about former players who could follow in his footsteps on the touchline, Guardiola was direct in naming his picks.

'I think Gundogan will be a good manager... Busquets will be a good manager. I knew Xabi Alonso would become a good manager.'

The statement brings together three players who played important roles in elite teams and who, during their careers, played in roles that demanded game reading, tactical understanding and the ability to organise collective actions.

The choice of names follows the central idea presented by the manager. For Guardiola, experience as a midfielder can offer an especially favourable base for those who want to lead a team. That is because the position requires involvement at different moments of the match, in both attacking build-up and defensive organisation, as well as a constant understanding of the positioning of team-mates and opponents.

Guardiola explained why he sees an advantage in players who operate in that area. In the Catalan's view, the role demands a reading that goes beyond individual participation, as the midfielder needs to understand how the team moves and what each moment of the match requires.

'I think midfielders have an advantage because they need to have a more global understanding of the game' - he said.

The manager deepened his reasoning by drawing a comparison with forwards. 'They have to make the team play and understand which areas to defend. A forward often just thinks: "I am going to score a goal, and that is it."'

The observation is not a criticism of forwards, but highlights the difference in responsibilities between the positions.

While a forward can concentrate much of his performance on finishing and the pursuit of goals, the midfielder needs to follow the collective dynamic, identify spaces, take part in ball circulation and understand the movements required to protect the team without possession.

The three names cited by the manager have trajectories that help explain his assessment. Gundogan worked with Guardiola at Manchester City, while Busquets was a key part of Barcelona during the period when Guardiola managed the team. Xabi Alonso, meanwhile, was coached by Guardiola at Bayern Munich.

What they have in common, beyond the position, is that all three built careers marked by the ability to interpret the game and make decisions in different tactical contexts.

In Alonso's case, Guardiola had already shown this perception before the former midfielder began his managerial career. The Spaniard retired as a player in 2017 and later rose to prominence in charge of Bayer Leverkusen, work that reinforced the bet made by his former manager.

Gundogan and Busquets are also examples of players who, through the experience accumulated in elite football, inspire Guardiola's confidence when it comes to a possible career in management.

#2013. Manchester United activate Bruno Fernandes contract extension clause until 2028

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have activated the one-year extension clause in Bruno Fernandes’ contract, ensuring their captain remains at Old Trafford until June 2028.

The Portuguese midfielder’s previous agreement was due to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season, but United have now exercised their option to keep him for another 12 months, according to Sky Sports.

The decision comes after Bruno Fernandes rejected two offers of a new long-term contract, with discussions between the player and the club having stalled in recent weeks.

Bruno Fernandes confirmed earlier this week that Manchester United had offered him fresh terms but insisted that he did not consider the current situation at the club suitable for contract negotiations.

The Portuguese manager wants United to direct their energies on the club’s current situation rather than his contract.

United helped themselves as well with the extension clause. They have now taken away that pressure of Fernandes negotiating a pre-contract deal with overseas clubs which he would have been free to do from January 1. The clause removes that immediate possibility and gives the club some control over his future.

Bruno Fernandes has attracted interest from several clubs in Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Italy but has repeatedly chosen to remain at Manchester United. He has insisted previously that he has unfinished business at Manchester United and wants to win trophies here.

Since arriving from Sporting CP in January 2020, he has become one of the club’s most influential players, scoring 115 goals in 343 appearances across all competitions. He was also appointed captain in 2023. Although his individual accolades have been called out by former winger Ashley Young as selfish, Bruno Fernandes remains United’s biggest attacking threat.

Despite the contract extension, it does not mean a new long-term agreement has been reached. Both Fernandes and United are understood to be comfortable returning to negotiations at a later stage, with their immediate priority being to improve the club’s current position.

#2011. £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Some surprised faces then when Moyes said later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”

The game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes said that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”

In the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

De Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender said: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and showed that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l

"Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young says that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev

Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh

Dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

There will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6

Tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

Spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a big chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

De Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

Johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

That opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

That was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

"What a chance this was!"Brennan Johnson had the chance to put Everton in front against his former club 😯 pic.twitter.com/fUi7t6hX7t

Everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

What is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

Antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors currently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

George does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

Spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

We are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

An uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

There will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

There has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

That is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

Tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

Gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Big question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

Spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

"Solanke is a crucial player"Roberto De Zerbi on the importance of Dominic Solanke being fit for Spurs 💪 pic.twitter.com/FNWNsTWdt8

Coventry City vs Brighton & Hove Albion (14:00)

Manchester United vs Manchester City (16:30)

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

🎧🫡 Thierno Barry ahead of today's clash in North London. pic.twitter.com/mwlsKH8Pid

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van de Ven, Van Hecke, Robertson; Tonali, Bentancur, Fernandes; Savio, Solankem, Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

After scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @SpursOfficial. COYB! ✊#TOTEVE pic.twitter.com/mOcCayRUfm

Roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#2009. Barcelona's Anthony Gordon 'stepped into Raphinha's shoes' against Sabah as Spanish media hail England international on historic night

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 09:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 09:29

Anthony Gordon scored twice in Barcelona's 4-1 win over Sabah in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

In doing so, Gordon made history - the forward has now scored six Champions League goals in Azerbaijan, which is the most any English player has netted in away games in one country in the tournament.

Four of the England international's goals in Azerbaijan came against Qarabag during his time with Newcastle United, before scoring twice against Sabah on Wednesday.

Lamine Yamal missed out through injury, while Raphinha was rested from the start, with Gordon joined by Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus in the final third, and all three found the back of the net.

As expected, Gordon's performance brought a lot of praise from the Spanish media.

6 - Anthony Gordon's six UEFA Champions League goals in Azerbaijan are the most any English player has scored in away games in one country in the competition. Tourist. https://t.co/7OfdYkdzch

AS were extremely positive about Gordon's performance, saying that the forward was 'vital' to Barcelona securing all three points in the Champions League.

Mundo Deportivo also highlighted how well he combined with Gabriel Jesus and Adeyemi in the final third of the field in the absence of Yamal and Raphinha.

La Vanguardia concentrated on how Gordon became the main player in the Barcelona attack and said that he was one of the main reasons why Hansi Flick's side were able to score four goals.

Culemania said that Gordon 'stepped into Raphinha's shoes', having netted twice in the absence of the Brazil international, who has scored 19 times in all competitions this season.

Gordon will never be the main man in the Barcelona attack due to the presence of both Yamal and Raphinha, but he has played an important supporting role this term.

The 25-year-old's numbers for this season are relatively solid, coming up with five goals and five assists in 17 appearances in all competitions.

In La Liga, Gordon has two goals and five assists in 12 appearances, while he has struck three times in five outings in the Champions League.

The forward will be looking to improve his goal total in Spain's top flight, but it has been a positive start to his Barcelona career for the former Everton youngster.

#2008. Manchester United target defender for January window but manager refuses to sell

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have leaked goals this season and Mauricio Pochettino is now set to get some names in January to address that.

United are reportedly considering several options at centre-back, with Calvin Bassey high on their shortlist. The 26-year-old has impressed since joining Fulham from Ajax in July 2023 for €22.5 million and has become an important figure at Craven Cottage. He currently captains Alvaro Arbeloa’s side.

The Nigerian defender has emerged as a potential target for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United look to address their defensive problems ahead of the second half of the season.

However, United have suffered a potential transfer setback after Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa made it clear that Calvin Bassey will not be allowed to leave during the January transfer window.

Alvaro Arbeloa has also confirmed that discussions are already taking place over a new contract.

“I am so happy with Calvin and obviously he is not on sale. No chance that he can leave this club in January. He is happy here, he is one of our captains and one of our leaders,” Arbeloa said about Bassey during his press conference.

Arbeloa believes the interest from other clubs reflects Bassey’s performances over time and is keen to keep him in his squad beyond the current season.

“You can see how he is playing and it’s normal that so many clubs are interested in him. It’s good for him and for us because it means he is performing really well.”

The Fulham manager also confirmed that the club are working on an improved contract for the Nigerian international.

“It’s very important for me as a coach, for the club and we are working on a new contract. I hope he can sign as soon as possible.”

Bassey’s current agreement runs until 2027, although Fulham have the option to extend it for another year. Amid the interest, the club is keen to reach fresh terms before his contract situation becomes a bigger issue.

Pochettino wants to strengthen his options, with the club sitting 19th in the Premier League table after 11 matches. United have a little budget for January and big names aren’t cheap to sign in that budget. Their interest in Bassey is understandable but given Arbeloa’s comment, United need a solid offer to get him in January.

But unless Fulham change their position or contract negotiations break down, United may have to look elsewhere for defensive reinforcements.

#2007. Kepa handed Arsenal opportunity to prove he can fill Raya’s boots against Dortmund

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

With David Raya out, Kepa Arrizabalaga has a great chance to prove that he is more than just an Arsenal cup keeper. Mikel Arteta needs to have confidence in his number two. He needs to ensure that he upholds the same high bar set by the starting keeper as Borussia Dortmund come to the Emirates.

Raya has been ruled out of tonight’s Champions League game following a shoulder problem which he picked up in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle United.

Whilst the initial diagnosis is good news, surgery is not required. Further tests will determine Raya’s recovery period.

As previously mentioned, Kepa will be stepping in for Raya at St James’ Park. Moreover, Arteta has stated his preferred choice of player in this situation. It seems that Illan Meslier will miss out on the opportunity to play this time.

As well as playing for Arsenal, the Spaniard has formerly played in the Champions League for Chelsea and Real Madrid. He has already appeared 14 times for the Gunners. Including in the league stage match which saw them beat Kairat Almaty.

Whilst Kepa has typically been second choice to Raya, his game time has mostly been in the EFL Cup. He will now need to prove himself as a trustworthy option for Arsenal should Raya be injured or otherwise unable to play.

As well as being a good goalkeeper, Raya is also good at passing and positioning. This in turn assists Arsenal in attacking from the back line.

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson has acknowledged the quality that Spanish goalkeepers have at creating good defensive and central positioning. This can frequently be an under-recognised yet important component in Arsenal’s build-up play.

Like Arsenal, Kepa will also have to remain calm when playing out from the back. Although Kepa does not necessarily need to replicate all of Raya’s qualities, he will need to have good decision-making skills as well as good communication.

Meslier is still in contention, having played in the Carabao Cup game against Fleetwood Town. Kepa has been Arsenal’s number two keeper in the Premier League and was able to rush on in for Raya when he was substituted at Newcastle.

It does seem that Kepa is the obvious option, and he can further cement his position in Arteta’s team.

Arsenal’s schedule is demanding. They are playing Manchester City on a Sunday and there are also worries about Raya’s fitness. So far, the club has not yet received medical information on Raya’s status.

Then there is Dortmund. They have already secured victories in their first four games in the Champions League and are level on points with Arsenal in the league section.

Kepa does not have a great deal of flexibility. Arsenal require the new goalkeeper to offer them security.

In case Raya needs more time to recover, it is necessary for Arteta to be able to guarantee that there is an effective replacement.

For Kepa, it is equally an opportunity to prove that he can assume this leadership position for the team during important moments.

#2006. Chelsea’s interest in Alex Scott remains despite Bournemouth transfer stance

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

The Blues had a £64m bid rejected during the summer, but their interest has continued into the new season. According to Matt Law of The Telegraph, Chelsea are at the front of the queue of clubs monitoring the 23-year-old.

Bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

The midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. He impressed during the 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia but was withdrawn after 70 minutes. Subsequent examinations revealed a quadriceps problem, with BBC Sport reporting that he could miss six to eight weeks.

His absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

Chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a new contract.

#2005. Chelsea make early move for Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

#2004. Arsenal waste chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back to claim Emirates point

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal failed to improve their Champions League prospects after a disappointing 1-1 game against Borussia Dortmund in which they lost their initial lead.

Despite Viktor Gyökeres’ spectacular goal, Mikel Arteta’s men allowed Maximilian Beier to level just after the halftime break. Although Arsenal were presented with several good scoring opportunities, they continually lacked composure in front of goal.

Despite winning their first three league phase games, it was an expensive night for Arsenal. They have maintained their perfect record in Europe, but for just the second time in the league phase at the Emirates, the Gunners have lost points.

Arteta will also be interested to see how much effort his team expended in their pursuit of a winning goal against Manchester City on Sunday.

Arsenal began confidently and quickly forced Dortmund to defend. Noni Madueke was troublesome on the right-hand side, and although Christos Tzolis was presented with a great chance, he failed to score from a cross.

Just ten minutes in, Madueke played a ball into the path of Gyökeres some 25 yards out. The Swedish forward then fired a curling shot over Gregor Kobel into the net.

A stunning goal from Arsenal’s forward was just what they required. Unfortunately, they were then unable to follow up this positive play.

Despite Tzolis’ effort prompting a save from Kobel, Madueke failed to score from the ball’s subsequent deflection. Likewise, Declan Rice was presented with a good opportunity when Martin Ødegaard set him up in a neat fashion.

Despite dominating play in the first half, Arsenal made a number of poor concluding decisions. Piero Hincapié failed to score from a good position, and Gyökeres also shot high from another good play.

Dortmund did not produce much throughout the game. However, Kepa Arrizabalaga did well to save from Joane Gadou in added time.

Arsenal should have gone into half-time with a more comfortable advantage. Instead, they gave the visitors a route back into the contest.

Shortly after play resumed, Beier failed to score despite being presented with a great chance following a low cross into the six-yard area.

Despite Arsenal successfully weathering that period of pressure, Dortmund soon retaliated. Gadou broke through the middle and passed to Beier, who then rounded Gabriel before coolly beating Kepa in the 55th minute.

Arsenal then faced a tougher challenge as they sought to add a second goal against increasingly confident Dortmund.

Arteta brought on Eberechi Eze, and the player quickly became involved. However, his shot was deflected just over the bar.

Continuing to trouble Dortmund, Madueke saw a header from Ødegaard also fly wide. A shot from Guirassy, also deflected, hit the post, and Rice then shot wide on the other side after Eze had provided an assist for him.

Despite having 29 shots at goal, the Gunners failed to make inroads. William Saliba, too, warmed up on the touchline and then did not play. Arteta continued with his existing defensive line.

Whilst Arsenal had much to be commended for in their attacking play, especially in the first half, good chances are of little use if they are not then converted.

Although Arteta will recognise that he should have secured three points, Dortmund have taken a well-earned point away from north London. Now, Arsenal need to swiftly refocus on Sunday’s game against Manchester City.

#2003. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#2001. Arsenal injury latest: Arteta faces selection headache as crucial fixtures approach

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could not have been in a more difficult position to suffer multiple key player injuries. Mikel Arteta will face a busy period with a Manchester City visit to the Emirates on Sunday and then in December face Tottenham and Real Madrid.

Although David Raya, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are all sidelined due to injury, Arteta has separate issues to deal with for each. However, the timing of their injuries is especially annoying.

The good news is that William Saliba is back in contention. But Arsenal can’t expect a select group of players to magically fix all of their issues. Over the coming weeks the true strength of the squad will be put to the test.

Raya is currently the most affected player. He suffered a shoulder injury while challenging William Osula in the 2-2 draw against Newcastle. As a result, he was also absent for the Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund.

Whilst there had been initial concerns over how long Raya would be out for, scans showed that there was no need for him to undergo surgery. Arteta has called the preliminary reports positive. However, he has yet to state if Raya will play against City.

Kepa Arrizabalaga has stepped in for Dortmund, but Arsenal are affected by the absence of their preferred keeper. Raya is reliable and composed and has great passing ability.

These attributes will be of value especially when facing City’s potent attack. Although Kepa has top-level experience, it is by no means a game that Arteta would prefer to be playing with an unstable goalkeeping situation.

Raya may be available again either on November 29 or when facing Brentford on December 2. Much will hinge on the progress of his shoulder in the days ahead.

Arguably, though, Saka’s injury represents a bigger worry. He was sidelined after hurting his quadriceps in a match against Bayern Munich on 21st October.

Arteta has previously suggested that it will take around eight weeks for Saka to make a full recovery. 20th December provides a possible return date, but there are no assurances that he will be fit to play at this time.

We have already analysed how important Saka is to Arsenal – both as a creator and in scoring and providing width. The new right winger will need to be able to create key moments in close games.

As well as losing Saka, Zubimendi is also set to be out for a number of weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem during his Spain duty. He may be available for the December 13 game against Bournemouth.

Without Zubimendi, Arteta will need to make further decisions regarding his midfield. Like Saka, Zubimendi is good at maintaining good structure, and this is key to Arsenal’s game. Finding a suitable replacement will not be an easy task.

There is some good news. Saliba has overcome his back issue and is once again in the squad. In addition, Max Dowman has served his 3-game ban.

Saliba’s return is particularly timely with City’s attacking threat heading to the Emirates. Arsenal need stability at centre-back, especially if Raya is unavailable.

Arteta still has decisions to make. Although there is not a great deal of time, Arsenal do not always find suitable substitutes. The squad is deep enough to still challenge, it will be in these next games that it will become apparent how much Arsenal miss key players.

On the face of it West Ham have too few options in key areas of the pitch, meaning that despite their ineffectiveness, the same payers have to be utilised again and again.

Joel Piroe, after another anonymous evening, will probably get selected to start at Saturday simply because of the options available: Neither Taty Castellanos who was invisible in his 10 minutes last night nor Pablo Felipe who is not even making Parker’s squad offer a better option as potential goal scorers. So Piroe’s ineffectiveness is set to continue.

The same applies in the case of  right back Joel Veltman: Albeit through Kyle Walker Peters‘ injury, Scott Parker has very little option but to start the Dutchman again, despite his pretty universally condemned performance at Fratton Park.

Veltman- unable to add much to West Ham’s offensive capabilities

Footballfancast.com  single out Veltman for special mention:

“The Dutchman, who is averaging 0.5 key passes and 0.1 dribbles per game, was once again ineffective in possession against Portsmouth before being substituted in the 62nd minute.

Veltman has never produced more than three assists in a season in his career and has not assisted more than one league goal in a season since the 2016/17 campaign with Ajax, which shows that he is an even bigger problem [than Piroe] as he does not have relevant experience to suggest that he will turn things around.

Parker must, now, drop the defender to the bench to explore his options in that area of the pitch, as the Hammers need more on the ball from the player in that position moving forward.”

Can’t really argue with that but unless Scott Parker is prepared to start Arne Engels as an emergency right back then the Hammers boss is fresh out of options until Walker Peters recovers.  Veltman was the free signing designed to give West Ham cover in the event of injury. Just an observation but does seem a trend when Walker Peters is absent, that Bowen hugs the touch line more, knowing his full back is not going to overlap or assist him in the way in which Walker Peters can.

Time, then, for anxious glances to the treatment table to see how Walker Peter’s recuperation from his thigh muscle issue is going.

#1999. Arsenal must seize title-race opportunity as Paul Merson questions Manchester City’s chances

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have the chance to put Manchester City’s Premier League title hopes under serious pressure this weekend. And with Pep Guardiola’s side already six points behind, this is an opportunity Mikel Arteta cannot afford to waste.

Paul Merson believes another City defeat could effectively end their title challenge. That might sound dramatic in November, but the gap is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

Arsenal welcome City to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, sitting top with 28 points from 11 matches. Their visitors have collected 22 points and gone four consecutive league games without a win.

The Gunners have been diligently building on this lead and can now add to the misery of one of their main competitors.

But Arsenal must be wary of thinking that Manchester City will continue to find life difficult. In fact, Guardiola’s men often thrive in such situations.

Whilst Merson has not ruled out City’s attacking prowess, two players in Rayan Cherki and Jérémy Doku have the ability to turn games around.

However, it is in City’s defensive phase, where more alarm bells should be ringing. The back-line has appeared susceptible and has consequently been exploitable.

And that is where Arsenal must show steel.

Arteta’s team have only scored seven goals in 11 Premier League games, compared to City’s 14. Much can be said from this stat alone.

Whilst Arsenal have based their title aspirations on great defensive organisation, City have failed to merge their potent attack with the structure that Guardiola requires.

Rather than passively allowing City to attack, the Gunners should exploit the instability in their opposition’s defence. Arsenal are more than capable of capitalising on these openings.

Psychologically, City are well aware that they cannot afford to continue to trail. In addition, if Arsenal dominate the early stages of the game, then City may well become even more desperate.

However, we must not underestimate Guardiola. City have previously turned around games that had gone against them. Arsenal need to ensure this does not happen here.

Merson’s comment that City stands virtually no chance of success following further failure is also quite an assertion.

Arsenal do already appear to have found their feet and can continue to accrue points thanks to their solid defence.

Whilst it would be unwise to totally dismiss City, Guardiola’s side does have sufficient quality to enable them to embark on a successful winning streak. And this cannot be switched off by one result.

As well as having issues to address, Arsenal have also shown problems scoring recently – both in draws with Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund. Against Dortmund, despite having good build-up play, the Gunners were especially frustrated as they failed to score from good opportunities.

And this cannot happen again when they face City.

Whilst this game may not decide the title race, there are still many games left to play, and Arsenal will also go through their own tough periods.

However, the significance of Sunday’s game should not be downplayed. A win would put nine points between the Gunners and City and further entrench Arsenal’s lead at the top.

It will also compel Guardiola’s men to come from behind.

Despite Merson perhaps being willing to dismiss City, Arsenal must ignore such punditry. They must then go on and produce a good game, seize their opportunities and capitalise on their lead.

#1997. Liverpool: With Isak and Wirtz, the Reds’ transfer business takes off a year late

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 09:44

During the 2025 summer transfer window, Liverpool broke the bank, spending £410m.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz were the two most expensive signings, as the Swedish striker arrived for £123m (€145m) and the German attacking midfielder for £106m (€125m). But for many months, the two most expensive recruits in the club's history failed to live up to expectations.

In his first season at Liverpool, Wirtz scored seven goals and provided 10 assists in 49 games, but his impact was largely disappointing. Isak, for his part, barely played (four goals and one assist in 22 games) because of a fractured fibula. That summer 2025 transfer window was thus described as 'the worst transfer window in Premier League history'.

Both attackers were therefore expected to deliver in their second season at Liverpool, with new manager Andoni Iraola arriving.

The momentum is completely different at the start of this campaign, as the 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night in the Champions League illustrated perfectly. Isak scored twice, while Wirtz also found the net.

The Swede is rediscovering the efficiency that made his reputation at Newcastle United. He now has ten goals in all competitions in 16 games and has just scored in six consecutive away games for Liverpool. The 27-year-old is establishing himself as the number nine Liverpool had long been waiting for.

On Wednesday night, Isak was asked about when he would be back at his best level: 'It is always difficult to say, but I can definitely say that I feel good, the team is in a good rhythm, that is the most important thing' - he said.

After a season of adaptation to English football, in which he struggled to have an impact in the final third and to be decisive, Wirtz is in excellent form.

Still deployed as a number 10, the 23-year-old German has scored four goals and provided five assists in 17 games in all competitions for Liverpool.

His November has been excellent: three goals and two assists in three games for Liverpool, as well as three goals in two games for the German national team. Wirtz appears to have digested his huge transfer and to be ready to shed his 'flop' label at Liverpool.

#1996. Now at least 7 Brighton players set to miss Newcastle United match after latest blow

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has been hit by yet another injury ahead of facing Matthias Jaissle and his Newcastle United team on Sunday in the Premier League.

The Seagulls were in action on Thursday night before lining up against Newcastle United.

The south coast club playing Universitatea Craiova in the UEFA Conference League.

Fabian Hurzeler needs as many players available as possible as he looks to compete in both Europe and the domestic competitions.

In the 39th minute of last night’s match, the Brighton boss saw Matt O’Riley on the end of a really poor challenge from Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu, who was then sent off after VAR review.

O’Riley tried to carry on but had to be replaced at the break and Fabian Hurzeler admitted after the match that it doesn’t look good for the Denmark international. The Brighton Head Coach revealing that the player’s ankle was very swollen.

This looks set to make it at least seven Brighton players ruled out of the Newcastle United match.

Malik Yalcouye was the latest long-term injury to hit the Seagulls ahead of last night’s game, whilst also ruled out are Kaoru Mitoma (knee), Stefanos Tzimas (thigh), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Zadok Yohanna (thigh).

Making it at least now seven Brighton players set to miss the Newcastle United match, as Joao Costinha is suspended after having been sent off during the 2-0 defeat at Hull City last weekend.

Other than the new injury for Fabian Hurzeler to deal with though, there wasn’t a lot of encouragement for Newcastle United from Brighton having this extra fixture to deal with ahead of Sunday.

The weak Conference League is very different to the demands of the Champions League.

Fabian Hurzeler was able to make eight changes and the Seagulls still cruised to victory against this weak Romanian opposition.

Only Maxim De Cuyper, Pascal Gross and Chema Andres stayed in the team from their Premier League defeat against Hull City and once they took the lead inside three minutes the result was never in doubt.

They were two up after 33 minutes and then when the opposition went down to ten men it was easy street for the Brighton players. The final score ended up 4-0 but if they had really needed a bigger scoreline, who knows what it could have been if they had went all out in this game, rather than having both eyes on Newcastle United less than 72 hours later.
