#1995. Paris Saint-Germain vs. Lorient - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 09:45, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:21

Winless against Lorient in two years, Paris Saint-Germain welcome the 10th-placed visitors to Parc des Princes for Saturday's matchday 12 clash.

The defending Ligue 1 champions' 12-match winning streak was halted by Roma on Wednesday, but they now aim to extend their sequence of eight consecutive top-flight victories.

PSG had maintained a perfect record across all competitions for nearly three months before Roma visited in the Champions League in midweek, with the Serie A side battling to a 2-2 draw on matchday five.

That result ended the Parisians' four-match European winning streak, although Luis Enrique's men remain second in the league-phase standings and firmly inside the coveted top-eight places that guarantee last-16 qualification.

Returning to league action should please supporters, who have watched their side claim eight consecutive victories since losing to Monaco at the start of September, albeit with only three clean sheets.

However, eagle-eyed observers will note that the Red and Blues have won only one of their last five meetings with Lorient across the past four years, with three of the last four encounters ending level.

Another draw would please Paris FC, Lille and Lyon, who trail the capital club by three, five and six points respectively as the Ligue 1 title race begins to take shape.

Alexandre Dujeux therefore aims to prevent Lorient's first defeat in this fixture since April 2024; however, his own five-match winless record against PSG and four consecutive losses to Enrique are ominous signs for the 50-year-old manager.

An indifferent run of results further undermines confidence in Les Merlus extending their unbeaten sequence in this fixture, with the Brittany-based club winning only one of their last four league matches.

Admittedly, only one of those matches ended in defeat, a 2-0 home loss to Brest, while their solitary victory during that period came away at Le Havre.

However, that early-November success offers limited encouragement given that it came against the division's bottom side, who have collected a paltry two points from 11 matches.

Their overall away record is more encouraging, with Dujeux's team conceding just twice across five matches on the road, both in September's 2-1 defeat to Le Mans, while keeping clean sheets in the other four.

Another shutout would make Lorient the first team since Monaco in November last year to prevent PSG from scoring, a feat far easier said than done.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue are both sidelined with ACL injuries for PSG's fixture on Saturday.

Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos are pushing for their first starts since last month's 4-2 victory over Barcelona, although Enrique may be tempted to retain the centre-back partnership of Ilya Zabarnyi and Willian Pacho.

Ferran Torres remains the capital club's leading Ligue 1 scorer with five goals, while Achraf Hakimi, Senny Mayulu and Marquinhos have three apiece.

Lorient have shared the goals around this season, with nine different players finding the net for the Brittany-based visitors.

Only Jean-Victor Makengo has scored more than once for Les Merlus, leaving Dujeux searching for someone to step up at Parc des Princes.

The visitors' prospects are further weakened by the absence of Panos Katseris, with a muscle injury ruling their leading goal provider out of this weekend's encounter.

Isaak Toure (groin) and Bandiougou Fadiga (muscle) are also sidelined for the 10th-placed side on matchday 12.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:

Safonov; Hakimi, Pacho, Marquinhos, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Godts

Mvogo; Adjei, Talbi, Obaretin; Sylla, Cadiou, Ebong, Kouassi; Makengo, Bernardeau; Tosin

Lorient's four clean sheets from five away matches suggest that PSG may need patience, particularly against opponents who have repeatedly frustrated them in recent meetings.

However, the visitors' limited scoring threat and Katseris's absence should allow Enrique's men to sustain pressure and eventually secure a ninth consecutive league victory.

#1994. Why were thousands of Sunderland fans banned from their latest European match?

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

I turned on the TV on Thursday night and I was puzzled, why were thousands of Sunderland fans banned from their latest European match?

The Mackems playing at the Stadium of Light in the Europa League.

Only the fifth European home match in the club’s entire history and yet Sunderland fans conspicuous by their absence.

The moment I switched on, the camera was focused on loads of sections of the Stadium of Light that were totally empty, no Sunderland fans in them at all.

I thought maybe I hadn’t heard of some UEFA ban that had forced them to close large parts of their stadium.

However, when the camera then focused elsewhere, there were many many empty seats in the areas of the ground that were open.

The match was woeful, the quality shocking, the only excitement when the cameras went back to the stands.

It turns out the embarrassing number of empty seats would have been far worse but for loads of Jagiellonia Bialystok fans buying tickets amongst the Sunderland fans. Turns out the Polish team had seen their supporters banned from attending this match due to past misbehaviour.

This type of thing rarely ends well when you have a set of away fans banned and a home club that struggles to sell their tickets. Sure enough, the Police seemed to be having to wade into any number of sections to deal with friction between the Sunderland fans and the visiting supporters amongst them.

Away fans in the home end #SAFC https://t.co/CuaC6FUyVE

— Sunderland Limbs 𝕏 (@LimbsSunderland) November 26, 2026

The actual match ended in a 1-1 draw and from what I saw, Sunderland very lucky to get a point against Jagiellonia Bialystok. Amusing to hear the booing from the few Sunderland fans who were still there at the final whistle.

The excitement of playing in Europe for only the second time in the club’s entire history, 53 years since the only other time, is now well and truly wearig off.

Polish club Jagiellonia Białystok were not supposed to have any away fans at The Stadium of Light for their game at Sunderland tonight due to a UEFA Disciplinary ruling, but loads of them are in the home end… 🫣😭 https://t.co/hBU0w02hYb

— Football Away Days (@FBAwayDays) November 26, 2026

I just checked the crowds and whilst the Mackems got 46,861 for their Premier League match against Arsenal, their Europa League home games have gone 45,555 against AZ Alkmaar, 44,269 v Dinamo Zagreb, last night 37,658. Sunderland fans deserting their team and the club having to totally close large areas of the Stadium of Light.

#1993. Nick Woltemade agent quizzed on transfer claim ‘These reports are completely untrue’

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Nick Woltemade continues to make headlines.

The German international striker had a rollercoaster first season at Newcastle United, starting off in great form and then a bit like the team overall, found things more difficult as the 2025-26 campaign progressed and a 58 game season was far too much for a small squad to deal with.

A lot of nonsense written and spoken about Nick Woltemade with ridiculous claims he had been a total flop, despite having 14 direct goal involvements including scoring 11.

The decision was made for Nick Woltemade to spend the 2026-27 season with Juventus, Matthias Jaissle wanting to have pace as his main focus up front.

The hope being that a year of regular football in Italy will help Nick Woltemade improve his skill set, become better at holding the ball up, polish his goalscoring technique and so on. Helping him then to come back and be a bigger asset for the Newcastle United team, or command a significant transfer fee boosted by his time with Juventus.

Big Nick has had mixed fortunes with Juventus, not getting the amount of game time he would like (seven starts in all competitions, eight sub appearances) but doing very decently in the time he has spent on the pitch (five goals and three assists so far).

Last weekend with Juventus drawing 0-0 at home and booed off at half-time, Nick Woltemade was introduced for the second half and within 14 minutes had turned the game around, scoring one and then getting an assist. Juventus finally winning 4-0 at the end against Venezia and the United loan star picking up the MOTM award.

It was bench duties again last night, Nick Woltemade coming on in the second half with Juventus leading 3-1 against Omonia Nicosia in the second half and the Newcastle United loan striker helping his side to an eventual 4-1 victory.

A lot of daft transfer claims floating about and now the United striker’s agent has shot down one of the daftest.

Al-Maidan contacted Danny Bachmann, Nick Woltemade’s agent, to ask about media claims of Newcastle United doing a January 2027 swap deal, with 30-year-old Ivan Toney (reported to be on £20million a year/£400k a week, plus Toney has a court date to face in London after having been arrested and charged with an alleged serious assault in a nightclub) to come to United from Al Ahli and 24-year-old Nick Woltemade to join the Saudi club.

Danny Bachmann dismissing this speculation as laughable nonsense: “These reports are completely untrue.”

The player’s agent making clear what the obvious reality is: “The player’s future will be decided at the end of the season when he returns to Newcastle United. We don’t know yet whether he will stay or leave.”

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Interesting comments from this BBC Sport pundit on Newcastle United.

Chris Sutton speaking as United prepare to play their fifteenth match of the 2026-27 season.

Newcastle United up against Brighton in the Premier League.

Matthias Jaissle hoping to see his team build on that excellent second half performance and deserved point against league leaders Arsenal.

The BBC Sport pundit declaring ahead Sunday: “I was at Newcastle’s draw with Arsenal last week and, in fairness to Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle, he changed things around at half-time and got his reward.”

Chris Sutton adding: “Jaissle needed that half of football, because I don’t think the Newcastle fans have been too convinced by his approach, but this is another very tough game for him.”

The BBC Sport pundit with zero doubts though for what will happen with Newcastle United this weekend, forecasting a 3-1 defeat at the Amex Stadium: “Brighton probably still can’t believe they lost to Hull last week – but lightning is not going to strike twice.”

You can’t disagree with Chris Sutton predicting Sunday as a home victory.

Brighton are huge favourites to win and they aren’t second in the table by accident.

However, last weekend showed just how unpredictable football can be.

Brighton totally dominated Hull City but then suffered a late red card and two goals for the home side to beat the Seagulls.

At St James’ Park, Arsenal totally dominated the first half and led at the break, yet in the end were lucky to escape with a point after Newcastle United were by far the better team in the second 45.

#1990. Leeds United news: Whites midfielder 'close' to signing new contract following dramatic 2026 turnaround

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 09:57

Leeds United have reportedly moved towards agreeing a contract extension for midfielder Ao Tanaka.

The Japan international has been a key part of Daniel Farke's side this season and started as the Whites smashed Chelsea by a 4-1 scoreline at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League last weekend.

Leading the line for the visitors in West London, Dominic-Calvert-Lewin is also supposedly on the verge of putting pen to paper on fresh terms at Elland Road, with Leeds closing in on the striker's renewed signature.

Losing just two matches in the top flight so far this term, Leeds are currently occupying seventh position in the Premier League standings, with the Yorkshire giants targeting European qualification.

Aiming to record three straight league wins for the first time this campaign, Farke's side will be the heavy favourites on Saturday afternoon, when they welcome former Championship foes Coventry City to Elland Road.

According to Sky Sports News, Leeds are moving decisively ahead of a busy festive period on the pitch, with the European hopefuls aiming to resolve the long-term futures of Calvert-Lewin and Tanaka.

The report states that the Whites are closing in on a contract extension for Japanese midfielder Tanaka, whose current deal at Elland Road expires at the conclusion of the 2027-28 domestic cycle.

It is understood that Farke's side have offered the ex-Fortuna Dusseldorf man an extra 12 months of contract security, meaning that he is set to be committed to the cause until June 2029.

At the beginning of the calendar year, there was a real question mark over whether Tanaka had a future in the first-team ranks of Leeds, who were comfortably avoiding a relegation battle without the 28-year-old in their starting XI.

However, the engine-room enforcer has since fought his way back to the front of the plans for the Whites, with the midfielder starting nine of the club's 11 Premier League fixtures in 2026-27 so far.

Given the positive trajectory of Leeds over the past few years, it is no surprise that contract extensions are the talk of the town at the moment, with the club's hierarchy keen to tie their best assets down.

On the pitch, Tanaka and Calvert-Lewin have been key to the first-team progression at Elland Road, with the Whites looking set to establish themselves as a Premier League regular over the coming years.

Bringing Leeds back up from the Championship in 2025, head coach Farke is also in line for a new contract, with the German tactician certainly deserving of such a reward in the near future.

#1988. Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”

What an important week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães said. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”

These are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”

Raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

Mikel Arteta launched a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

“In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” said Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

“I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

“You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

“I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. We had really good periods but didn’t score and after that they can suffocate you especially when they decided to be really physical and very direct and we had to overcome a situation that in my opinion was absolutely unacceptable at this level. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

“Are you surprised? Are you surprised? No. OK.

“Ezri does nothing. Just watch it. We have a lot of cameras and VAR, and we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing,” he added.

“I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”

Guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

I’m so upset – it’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of a season, of the championship. I’ve seen it 10 times, to make sure, because I saw it live and said ‘It’s not possible at this level it can be a penalty’. Because it’s a judo roll, that’s what it is. It cannot happen.

I’ve been in football for 27 or 28 years - it’s not a penalty in any game, in any league, in any context.

Sunderland are a really, really good team and I don’t want to take any credit away from them. It’s been extremely tough and I’m really happy that we’ve done it.

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league" 😳Mikel Arteta reflects on Arsenal's 2-0 win over Sunderland 👀@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/2BUZILexk3

I feel very good. It was a beautiful goal and a beautiful moment for me and my family.

It’s a very good place to score! Everyone knows my history at Newcastle; now I’m trying to create more history with Arsenal.

[Is David Raya the best goalkeeper in the world?] Definitely. This guy’s an unbelievable player.

What a goal! And especially the time he scored. Coming to this place is so difficult but we dealt with it very well.

It’s a big moment, especially at 0-0 away from home, and they were on top of us at the time.

Arsenal have won nine Premier League games in a row for the first since the Invincible season of 2003-04.

Three away games for Arsenal this season, three wins and three clean sheets. Nobody does it better. The Arsenal players will sleep well tonight because Sunderland made them work extremely hard for the three points.

The match was decided by a dramatic three-minute period early in the second half. Enzo Le Fee’s penalty was superbly saved by David Raya; then the Arsenal substitute – and former Newcastle captain – Bruno Guimares slammed a spectacular goal.

Bukayo Saka confirmed victory with an injury-time penalty. Arsenal are top of the table with 12 points out of 12; good luck trying to catch them.

90+7 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 2 (Saka pen) Bukayo Saka’s penalty goes through the hands of the diving Roefs and into the net. That should be the last kick of the game.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

90+6 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 1 Saka is fouled by Reinildo, whose misery is compounded by a second yellow card.

Gabriel and Mukiele are booked for their part in that shoving match.

There’s a bit of pushing and shoving from players on both sides after a foul by Isidor on Guimaraes. Nothing much in it.

Sunderland have six minutes of added time in which to find an equaliser.

Arsenal substitution Mikel Merino for Martin Odegaard, presumably for his height at defensive set-pieces.

Big save from Raya! Xhaka takes a corner on the right, gets it back and curls another wicked ball into the six-yard box. Mukiele stretches to poke it towards goal and Raya paws the ball away. It loops up invitingly in front of goal - but then Raya is fouled by one of the Sunderland players charging desperately towards the ball.

A Sunderland corner loops up in the air and is volleyed acrobatically over the bar by Mukiele. That was a pretty good effort, and it only just cleared the bar.

Double change for Arsenal Eberechi Eze and Martin Zubimendi replace Christos Tzolis and... Declan Rice. He doesn’t look injured so it might just be workload management.

Brobbey pushes Gabriel over off the ball and is booked.

Disallowed goal Odegaard’s beautiful free-kick is headed in emphatically by Timber - but then the flag goes up for offside. Not much in it but the decision has been confirmed.

Sunderland substitution Malick Fofana replaces Thomas Meunier and creates a chance immediately with a thrilling run down the left. There’s an appeal for a penalty and then a close-range backheel from Mukiele that is blocked by Konsa.

Ballard clears off the line! Saka swings the resulting corner to the far post, where Havertz rises imperiously to head past Roefs. Ballard stoops towards his own goal and heads clear superbly. I’m not entirely sure Havertz’s header was on target but Ballard didn’t know that.

Moments later, Guimaraes curls just wide of the far post.

Fine save by Roefs! Arsenal cut Sunderland open on the break. Tzolis flicks a neat pass to Odegaard, who runs at a backpedalling defence and tees up Saka. His right-foot shot is beaten round the post by Roefs.

Eyebrows were raised at the £75m fee for Bruno Guimaraes, especially as he turns 29 in November, but Arsenal were willing to pay so much money because they knew the Brazilian was a sure thing. Only a player with serious experience of the Premier League could come into central midfield, off the bench, in a game like this and completely understand the tempo and flow of the game.

Sunderland substitution Wilson Isidor replaces Nilson Angulo.

Xhaka is booked for a sliding tackle on Guimaraes, though he got the ball and felt it was a clean challenge.

Chance for Arsenal Saka puts Havertz through on goal on the left side of the area. He eschews the shot and instead tries to find Tzolis with a square pass that is cut out by a Sunderland defender. Havertz may have been too selfless there.

Dan Ballard is booked - not sure whether it was a foul or for dissent.

The home fans have been stunned into relative silence by that double whammy. It was a mighty finish from Bruno Guimaraes.

58 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 1 (Guimaraes) A hammer blow from the former Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes! Sunderland looked set to go 1-0 up a moment ago; now they’re 1-0 down. Rice played a square pass to Guimaraes, lurking with intent just outside the D; he got the ball out of his feet and whipped an unstoppable curler into the top corner. What a way - and time, and place - to score your first Arsenal goal.

54 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 0 A long throw from the left is claimed by David Raya - but the referee points to the spot after a wrestling manoeuvre by Konsa on Ballard!

Arsenal are furious, and that probably wouldn’t have been given last season, but clubs were told at the start of the season that wrestling would be penalised.

Gabriel goes down holding his jaw and claims he was elbowed by Ballard. VAR aren’t interested and the referee tells an irritated Gabriel to leave the field for one minute.

Konsa makes an important challenge on the relentless Brobbey, as does Gabriel on Le Fee a few seconds later. Sunderland keep pushing and Sadiki rakes a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Chance for Sunderland A long throw from the right isn’t cleared by Arsenal, and eventually Meunier hits a snapshot that is kicked away instinctively by David Raya. That’s a pretty good save.

Jurrien Timber and Bruno Guimaraes, who is popular in these parts, replace Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Tzolis’s deep cross is headed back into the six-yard box by Saka. Havertz stoops towards the ball but is beaten to it by Xhaka, a crucial bit of defending and the last action of a hard-fought, goalless first half.

Ben White has a groin problem and is going to be replaced by Jurrien Timber, either now or at half-time.

Xhaka’s dangerous corner is punched back to him by Raya. He picks out Le Fee, who drags a shot wide of the near post from 20 yards. Sunderland’s belief is growing.

Angulo goes down in the Arsenal area after a challenge from the side by White. Play continues and Meunier’s speuclative shot deflects behind for a corner.

Sunderland have been terrific in this first half.

Mikel Arteta is booked for encroaching outside his technical area. He responds by sticking his thumb up at the fourth official.

Mikel Arteta receives a yellow card for stepping out of the technical area 😅📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/xDlnL1B9MY

Arsenal are yet to score from a set piece this season. Their supporters have used that fact as evidence they are not as reliant on corners as their critics say, but the truth is that it will bother Arteta and set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. This is the sort of cagey game in which Arsenal so often made the breakthrough from a set piece last season.

Sunderland break through Mukiele, who charges into space and rifles a low drive that is blocked by Gabriel on the edge of the area.

The resulting corner leads to a brief VAR check for an Arsenal penalty after a bit of a wrestling match between Calafiori and Brobbey. Nothing given.

Good save by Roefs Saka curls a cross towards Havertz, who does well to control it on the chest while facing away from goal. He waits for the ball to bounce and hooks an imaginative shot that is fingertipped over by Roefs. Good save.

Chance for Arsenal Tzolis plays a nice pass down the side of the area for Odegaard. He cuts the ball back to Havertz, who screws a first-time shot over the bar. It was a slightly awkward chance because of the angle of Odegaard’s pass.

Reinildo is booked for a foul on Saka. The home fans are getting annoyed with what they perceive as diving from some of the Arsenal attackers: “Same old Arsenal, always cheating” is the chant of choice just now. Odegaard also went down a moment ago after a foul from Angulo.

Gabriel strides forward from defence and sweeps a left-foot shot from 25 yards. It’s a good effort that fades just wide of the far post with Roefs scrambling across his line.

Sunderland will be really pleased with the first quarter. They’re defending solidly and look a threat on the break, thanks in part to some outstanding hold-up play from Brian Brobbey. Saka’s volley is the only shot on target at either end.

Chance for Sunderland Brobbey does brilliantly to hold the ball and find Le Fee, who is fouled on the left wing by Gabriel. That allows Sunderland to send the centre-backs forward - and one of them, Dan Ballard, almost opens the scoring!

Xhaka curled a sensational ball around the Arsenal defence towards the far post, where the ball bounced up awkwardly and was knocked wide by either Ballard or Mukiele, who flew in at the far post. Ballard would have had an easier chance had Mukiele not got in the way.

Chance for Arsenal Saka mishits a volley straight at Roefs from close range after running onto a penetrative pass from Rice. It wasn’t an easy ball to take on the volley - Rice hit it very firmly - but Saka would usually do better.

The pattern of the game has been established, with Arsenal dominating the ball and Sunderland picking their moments to press and then counter-attack.

Looks like it will be a good battle between Brian Brobbey and Ezri Konsa. Brobbey seems to be attaching himself to Konsa, rather than getting into a scrap with Gabriel.

Sunderland break promisingly down the right. Mukiele drives an angled low cross that only just evades Angulo at the far post.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

Enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

Arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

We’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

We know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

When will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the new £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Saturday night Gunners ❤️‍🔥🤝 Presented by @deel

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

#1987. After moving from the Foxes exciting midfield prospect Christian Boothe signs Newcastle United professional contract

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

In late August, Christian Boothe was persuaded to move from Leicester City to Newcastle United.

The exciting teenage midfielder swapping the Foxes for the Magpies.

Now it has been revealed he has signed his first professional contract with Newcastle United on the day of his 17th birthday).

(ED: Players generally cannot sign a professional contract until their 17th birthday. Under The FA’s Rule C11, players must be 18 or over to enter a playing contract unless they are 17 and not in full-time education.)

A club statement on 28 August 2026 revealed that the young Leicester City starlet was one of three that Newcastle Unuted had persuaded to swap clubs as NUFC look to recruit the best young talent possible for the future: ‘Newcastle United can announce that promising youngsters Kyran Thompson, Christian Boothe and Kyle Healy-Matthews have joined the club’s Academy.  Thompson joins the club from Arsenal, with Boothe and Healy-Matthews arriving from Leicester City and West Ham United respectively.’

Having signed his Newcastle United pro contract, a now 17-year-old Christian Boothe reacting: “It is a surreal moment for me and my family, I’m so grateful to sign it with such a big club like Newcastle. I can’t wait to see what the future holds for me. I wanted to sign because there were better opportunities for different pathways into the first-team. I’m loving my time here. The name, Newcastle United, speaks for itself. Who wouldn’t want to join Newcastle? It’s a lovely club with so many good footballers that have played here. I’m also so lucky that I knew a few of the boys before I joined; Jayden (Kouossu), Muawiya (Ghanem) and Kyle (Healy-Matthews) as well because my brother played at West Ham. To have those friendships already definitely helped me to settle in.”

The exciting teenage midfield talent looking to take inspiration from Lewis Miley and Elliot Anderson: “You’ve seen the likes of Lewis and Elliot play for Newcastle’s first-team after coming through the Academy. I try to study their game and learn what I do differently to them and vice-versa, to try and follow in their footsteps. I’m really enjoying it at Newcastle so far and I think I’ve been performing well for the Under-18s. This season, I want to try and break into the Under-21s squad as well as train with the first-team. If I do get my shot with the first-team, it’s about making sure I express myself.”

Academy Director Steve Harper (pictured at the top of this article): “Christian has settled into life at Newcastle United really well since arriving last summer and we’re delighted to see him sign his first professional contract with the club. Joining a new environment always brings challenges, but he has adapted quickly, embraced the standards we expect and shown a strong commitment to developing his game. He’s worked hard to build relationships with his teammates and coaches, and that positive attitude has helped him make a strong start to his time here. This contract is recognition of the progress Christian has made so far, and we’re looking forward to continuing to support him as he develops and works towards achieving his potential.”

It is Brighton v Newcastle United up next.

Fabian Hurzeler and his Seagulls taking on Matthias Jaissle’s Magpies.

Brighton v Newcastle United has never featured a Premier League away win for United.

In more than 35 years we have seen only one win for Newcastle at Brighton, a 2-1 Championship victory in the 2016-17 season, featuring that astonishing Mo Diame wonder goal!

Since the 1991-92 season there have only been 12 of these Brighton v Newcastle United matches but it is still not a place high on the expectation list for NUFC fans.

Brighton are second top in the Premier League of course and whilst Newcastle United got that excellent 2-2 draw with Arsenal, Fabian Hurzeler and his team smashed them 3-0 at the Amex Stadium.

Brighton have a Premier League record this season of Played 11 Won 7 Drawn 1 Lost 3.

In all competitions, Brighton’s record is Played 19 Won 12 Drawn 3 Lost 4.

However, the very daunting stats only appear ahead of this Brighton v Newcastle United match when you look at how the Seagulls have got on home and away.

In their 11 away matches in all competitions, Brighton have won 5, drawn 2 and lost 4, scoring 17 goals and conceding 13.

In their 8 home matches (all competitions), Brighton have won 7, drawn 1 and lost none, scoring 27 goals and conceding only 1!!

In over three months, the 1-1 Premier League draw against Leeds on 5 September 2026 is the only time this season that Brighton at home have conceded a goal, failed to win and not managed to score at least two goals on home turf.

The challenge is on for Newcastle United.

#1983. This year’s Axel Disasi : Could defender loan rescue West Ham’s vulnerable back line?

Despite the ultimate failure of Chelsea loanee Axel Disasi to enable West Ham’s hapless defence to secure Premier League survival, most fans look back with a certain fondness at that brief period of optimism that coincided with the solid, committed defender’s arrival and the transformative effect he had on the Hammers’ fortunes.

Twelve months on and unbelievably, West Ham’s defence is in need of rescuing once again. Week in, week out (apart from a brief, one game ‘Morato’ interlude which Parker has inexplicably ditched), Kilman and Mavropanos prove they’re not fit for purpose as a solid, reliable centre back pairing meaning West Ham must again look to shore up the leaky back line in January – another loan on the cards then:

For West Ham, Heaven represents an opportunity to add a highly rated young defender to a squad looking to strengthen after a difficult campaign…For West Ham, a loan agreement could offer an opportunity to give Heaven regular senior football without requiring a major permanent investment immediately.

Is Ayden Heaven a better bet than Morato? Only if Scott Parker has the cojones to use him instead of his £40m flop

His development at the club could then determine whether a longer-term deal becomes realistic.”

Although different in age and career trajectory, the left footed centre back could revitalise West Ham’s defence in the same way that Axel Disasi managed last year, replacing the hesitant Maximilian Kilman who still has to earn about £39 million of his £40 million transfer fee.

Is Heaven the answer to West Ham’s woes? Who can tell: He’d 100% be an improvement though.

At 20, is he a significant upgrade on Morato or Golambeckis, either of whom would deprive more resilient than Kilman alongside Mavropanos? You’d think ‘not’.

Somehow each successive manager has continued making the same mistake and pairing the hapless duo together with predictably, the same results. If a loan of Ayden Heaven means West Ham are prepared to drop Kilman and split the centre back pairing of panic, then please, please let it happen, Koppen.

#1981. Man United urged to sign £62.8m midfielder to fix "phenomenal" transfer mistakes (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 10:16

Former Manchester United star Gordon Strachan - speaking exclusively to Sports Mole - has urged the Red Devils to sign a £62.8m midfielder to help correct their "phenomenal" transfer mistakes.

New Man Utd manager Mauricio Pochettino remains winless since replacing Michael Carrick following Wednesday's infuriating 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, in which the Red Devils fell behind, took the lead and were then pegged back in Portugal.

The four-goal stalemate marked the seventh game in a row that Man United had conceded at least two goals, and once again, the Red Devils' open midfield was exposed.

The pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo did not cover themselves in glory against Liverpool or Sporting, and the former is now suspended for RB Leipzig in December after being sent off towards the end of Wednesday's game.

Andrey Santos has also not yet had the desired impact since joining from Chelsea, while fellow 22-year-old Carlos Baleba has played just 397 minutes across seven appearances due to injury problems.

Speaking to Sports Mole via William Hill betting site, Strachan - who scored 36 goals in 198 games for Man United - has told the Red Devils hierarchy to make a move for Crystal Palace lynchpin Adam Wharton to help offset the "phenomenal" amount of money the club has wasted on under-performing players.

"Adam Wharton is one of my picks," Strachan said. "Elliot Anderson was also another one they should have gone for. Tielemans has been doing well in the Premier League for nearly 10 years, so they're buying somebody who's at the latter stage of his career. I might be wrong, I hope I'm wrong, and hopefully, he’s got another five or six years in him.

"And I've got to say, the world of football in England is full of the top teams, especially Chelsea, Spurs, bringing in players who sign for £40m, £50m, you go, who is he? There's just so many players like this now.

"You see some of these players, and you go, what has he done to deserve a £45m fee? Baleba, Santos, you’re picking up people for big fees, who have no reputation.

"Who's been brave here? Is this just a kind of cosy midfield? You could go back to Mason Mount for £40m - who actually signed this off to pay this amount of money for players?

"It’s just beyond belief the money that Man United have wasted. It's phenomenal. And that's from the recruitment not doing their work properly.

"They've got to start saying, what is my plan for the next 10 years at Man United? And how do we go about this? Arsenal were a bit like that five or six years ago. It wasn't anywhere near as bad a situation as Man United, but they stuck to their plan, and it paid off."

Data from the 2026-27 season does not paint Wharton in the most positive light compared to his Man United peers, given Crystal Palace's atrocious start to the campaign.

Indeed, the England international only leads Baleba, Tielemans, Santos and Mainoo on games played, crosses per 90 and accurate crosses per 90, while also winning the fewest duels and registering the lowest percentage of successful passes.

However, Wharton has committed the fewest fouls per 90 minutes of the quintet, and he has been dispossessed on the second-fewest occasions per 90 minutes, only behind Santos.

Thanks to Crystal Palace's perilous position in the Premier League table - Thomas Frank's men sit bottom of the rankings with just seven points from nine games - interested parties could pick up Wharton for a discount if the Eagles are relegated to the Championship.

The 22-year-old is valued at €75m (£62.8m) by Transfermarkt and has three years left on his Palace contract, but Man United may have to fend off competition from Liverpool and Chelsea to land him in 2027.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

#1980. All of the frustration, none of the magic | West Ham’s latest enigma

Watching last night’s woeful performance against Portsmouth unfold, I was struck by the similarity in playing style of one current West Ham winger with a previous playing enigma from whom West Ham could never seem to coax the best.

Triggered by the  irritation generated from watching Manor Solomon constantly check back, slow down play and then inevitably cut inside, I found myself comparing him with another West Ham winger who repeated the same trick ad nauseam.

Even on the one occasion when he was put clean through beyond his full back, by a brilliant pass from Ezra Mayers, Solomon got to the by line and – infuriatingly, checked back instead of trying to cross with his weaker foot.

And at that moment I thought “Saïd Benrahma” all over again.

The enigma that was Saîd Benrahma: at least he scored a few, created a few, and smacked a mean penalty past Fiorentina’s keeper in the summer of 2023.

‘Benny’ could at least create chances (and score a mean penalty) whereas Manor Solomon just runs down blind alleys, head down, inevitably slowing and cutting inside to use his right foot.

Exactly as, on numerous occasions in each game, the Algerian would check back, infuriatingly, and slow up play instead of pressing on to beat his full back on the inside or out. In that respect Solomon seems identical, disrupting West Ham’s flow, allowing defenders to reset and frustrating the bejesus out of supporters.

At least Benrahma could create and occasionally score: Solomon has, by the reckoning of westhamworld.co.uk, now played “1141 minutes for two goals and two assists, averaging a goal every 285 minutes”.

For whatever reason the Israeli clearly is a shadow of the player who helped fire Leeds to promotion and West Ham need to consign him to the same ‘rest and recuperation’ home in which Mads Hermansen has been sent to recapture his form.

Austbo at least has a shot on him and seems to be able to beat players inside and out: With the Norwegian there is the feeling that there’s more to come. With Solomon, exactly as Tottenham fans suggested, the fear is that his best days are long in the rear view mirror. Much like Saîd Benrahma, but without the trophy to show for it.

#1979. Liverpool ‘showing concrete interest’ in Bundesliga wonderkid Jurgen Klopp likes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a new contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

“I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”

With a contract currently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Liverpool, it has to be said, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”

The big issue facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

#1977. Bournemouth vs. Celta Vigo: How the Cherries could equal Chelsea, Leeds feat with Europa League victory

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 10:27

Bournemouth have prepared for their Europa League clash at Celta Vigo in the knowledge that they could smash even more history.

Marco Rose's side won just two of their opening eight competitive matches of the 2026-27 season, hinting that there could be a period of struggle following Andoni Iraola's departure to Liverpool.

However, with the Cherries set for a Celta Vigo challenge on Thursday night, it is clear that the Dean Court club are thriving, with the visitors to Spain sitting in fifth position in the Premier League standings.

A star of the current positive form, Evanilson has truly announced himself as an elite top-flight striker, netting seven goals and providing two assists in his past eight appearances, scoring in five consecutive league fixtures.

What makes Bournemouth's run even more impressive is that last season's star man Junior Kroupi has barely started a competitive match so far after recovering from a broken leg sustained over the summer.

Starting with a 3-0 Europa League success over Austrian side Sturm Graz on October 15, Bournemouth have recorded nine straight victories in all competitions across the Premier League, EFL Cup and European action.

That winning streak is the longest since the Cherries became a Football League club at the beginning of the 1923-24 season, showcasing how impressively the South Coast team are performing at the moment.

However, there are still more records to be achieved over the coming weeks, with Bournemouth aiming to become only the eighth team to record 10 straight competitive victories whilst playing in the Premier League.

Winning the Premier League during the 2016-17 campaign under Antonio Conte, Chelsea managed 10 wins in a row in all competitions, with that particular streak running from October 2016 until New Year's Eve 2016.

Leeds are the other club to post that exact number of wins in succession, with the Elland Road side completing the feat between August and October during the 1999-00 Premier League term.

The dominant force in English domestic football during the late 2010s and early 2020s, Manchester City are unsurprisingly the club with the most consecutive competitive wins as a Premier League side.

Under the expert stewardship of Pep Guardiola, the title-winning Citizens won 21 straight matches between December 2020 and March 2021, destroying Arsenal's previous record of 13 games in succession.

To match Man City's record, Bournemouth would need to secure victory in Spain on Thursday before winning every single match up to and including the trip to Brighton & Hove Albion on January 5.

I wrote yesterday that I was struggling for answers regarding how West Ham can address their current form. And then, like a lightning bolt, it all became a lot clearer to me!

Some players influence matches in ways that do not always show up in the highlights package. And West Ham have two such players, one of whom has been overlooked by Scott Parker.

The player overlooked is none other than Pablo Felipe.

Now, before we get ahead of ourselves, I’ve openly never been a big fan of the player. He barely scores any goals, looks slow and has missed some great opportunities in front of goal.

However, while Pablo Felipe may not always grab the headlines, the numbers indicate he is one of the most influential players in our squad.

When Pablo starts, West Ham score first in 83.6% of matches. Without him in the starting line-up, that figure plummets to just 18.2%. In football, scoring first can completely change the course of a game, making this a significant indicator of his influence.

The defensive numbers are equally striking. With Pablo on the pitch, the team have scored 16 goals while conceding only five. Without him, they have scored 19 but conceded 19. While the attacking output remains similar, the defensive stability and overall balance are clearly stronger when he plays.

“Staring Parker in the Face” West Ham’s Missing Link? The gaffer could do worse than select Pablo

This highlights something many supporters already recognise. Pablo’s value lies in his work rate, intelligent positioning, pressing and ability to knit the team together. He helps the side control matches, protects the defence and creates the conditions for others to shine.

With few options and players underperforming, Parker may look to reintegrate the Portuguese striker into the first-team set-up for the visit of Stoke City on Saturday.

The other player who deserves a place in the starting eleven is Tomáš Souček. Despite featuring for just 182 minutes across nine matches, he has already registered three goals and eleven shots. #1974. Křetínský’s Silence Is Becoming A Problem For West Ham

I think we’ve reached a point now where we need some more clarity from West Ham United about the future direction of the football club. Whilst I understand there is an overriding desire to get the Hammers promoted, something which has been described to us by club insiders as a priority, I’m increasingly concerned about how we intend to achieve it.

Because as things stand at the moment, West Ham appear rudderless. In fact, I’d go as far as to say we’re listing. We’re getting progressively worse, and there is a worrying lack of direction at the football club.

Whilst there may be a desire to reach a certain destination, I see very little from West Ham at the moment to suggest that we know the route. And that’s why I believe we really need to hear from Daniel Křetínský.

We’ve waited an awfully long time for the restructuring of West Ham’s shareholding to go through. And whilst Claret & Hugh reported earlier this month that the transactions had been completed, we’re still waiting for public confirmation from the football club.

Křetínský himself has indicated that he will engage with supporters once the share transaction has been finalised, but quite frankly, I don’t think that’s good enough anymore.

West Ham are in desperate need of leadership. Whatever the situation with his shareholding, Křetínský is already in a position of authority at the football club.

West Ham are still waiting for Daniel Kretinsky to address supporters

Whilst I don’t expect him to be shooting from the lip in the way David Sullivan used to, I do think he needs to provide some leadership, some direction and some communication with supporters as to what the actual plan is here.

Because almost everybody at every level of the football club, from the players right up to the very top, appears to be struggling.

Ideally, I’d like to know what the direction of travel is. What is the plan for West Ham United?

They want to take us forward, but how are they going to do that? What’s the plan for January? What’s the plan for investment?

We sold around £200m worth of players during the summer, we’ve yet to see the anticipated injection of funds from the shareholders, and we currently don’t look anything like a team capable of mounting a successful promotion challenge.

And that, by the club’s own admission, is supposed to be the number one priority.

As things stand, the team are getting worse and the club appear to be getting worse. I don’t think West Ham supporters are being unreasonable in wanting to know what the people running our football club intend to do about it.

#1973. ‘The only question is…’ – Chris Sutton gives emphatic Liverpool v Man United prediction

Chris Sutton has said he can ‘only see one result’ from Liverpool’s showdown against Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The home side go into the fixture 10 points and 14 places ahead of their arch-rivals, for whom this is a first game in charge for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds’ home record in the Premier League so far this season has been poor, with just one win from five, but victory today would see them close to within one point of third-placed Manchester City.

In his weekly Premier League column for BBC Sport, Sutton voiced his belief that the visitors won’t have any ‘new manager bounce’ at Anfield and has forecast Liverpool to win handsomely.

The former Chelsea striker wrote: ‘Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently – two draws and a win in their past three visits – but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

‘Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counterattack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

‘Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.’

Sutton has predicted a resounding 4-0 win for Liverpool, matching the scoreline from this fixture in April 2022.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Considering the form and league positions of the teams, objectively the Reds ought to go into this game as clear favourites. When fifth plays host to second from bottom in the Premier League, the former would naturally be expected to win.

However, the pundit referenced Man United’s good record at Anfield since the famous 7-0 drubbing in March 2023, and Liverpool were also widely expected to win on a couple of those occasions.

Pochettino has never lost his first match at any of the five clubs he’s previously managed, and Reds fans might naturally be wary that the players who effectively downed tools under Michael Carrick will suddenly have a spring in their step today.

The good news for Iraola is that he has a mostly fully-fit squad, with Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai overcoming minor issues over the past couple of weeks and Ryan Gravenberch available once more, and there were no fresh injury casualties over the international window.

The Liverpool head coach has had a reasonably good start to his reign but is still waiting on a genuine ‘statement’ victory. That would change if Sutton’s emphatic prediction comes to light, but we’re sure that every Kopite would gladly take a win by any means against our biggest rivals.

#1972. Luton Town vs Oxford United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 10:55, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:05

Two former Arsenal teammates come head to head on Saturday in League One as in-form Luton Town welcome high-flying Oxford United to Kenilworth Road.

Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.

More than six months after Luton Town narrowly missed out on a place in the League One playoffs last season, finishing just one point behind sixth-placed Leyton Orient, the Hatters have made a positive start to the 2026-27 campaign as they look to go one step better this time around.

Wilshere's side began the new season inconsistently and were sitting 16th after seven third-tier matches at the end of September, but have since enjoyed an impressive upturn in form, losing just once in the league across October and November, a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons at Stadium MK.

That run has seen Luton win six of their last eight league matches, while also progressing to the second round of the FA Cup and the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy, putting them firmly back in the playoff picture.

In fact, the Hatters could move into second place heading into the final month of the calendar year if they secure a ninth league victory of the season and other results go their way this weekend, with their recent form having lifted them more than 10 places into fifth and guaranteed them a place in the top six until at least their 17th league match next week, when they face struggling Blackpool.

A key factor behind their turnaround has been an improvement in front of goal, with Luton scoring 17 times in League One since the start of October, an average of more than two per game that has taken their overall tally to 29, a record bettered by just one side in the division.

As for the visitors, Oxford United make the 66-mile journey to Bedfordshire in similarly strong form and will be looking to move into December in the top two by recording a third consecutive victory.

The U's, led by former Wales midfielder Ramsey, have enjoyed a more consistent campaign than their upcoming opponents, having already moved into the top six by their seventh match of the 2026-27 season, when Luton were sitting 16th, and have continued to build on that strong start in recent weeks to climb to third.

Oxford head into their 15th league outing of the season with 29 points following eight wins, five draws and just one defeat, and they could move level on points with leaders Stockport County this weekend while still having two games in hand on Jimmy McNulty's side.

Although Oxford's FA Cup campaign came to an end at the first hurdle with a 1-0 home defeat to Stevenage, their form in the third tier has been exceptional, with no side in the top four divisions of English football losing fewer league matches than the U's.

Only Ramsey and Wilshere's former club Arsenal and League Two side Barnet have matched their tally of just one defeat.

While Luton have built their campaign around a clinical attacking unit, Oxford's promotion push has been underpinned by a strong defensive record, with only three sides in League One having conceded fewer than their 14 goals.

However, shipping three at home to Wycombe Wanderers last weekend, despite coming from three goals behind to secure a remarkable 4-3 victory, represented a rare blemish on an otherwise impressive defensive campaign.

The pair meet for the first time in just under two years on Saturday and will lock horns in a third-tier fixture for the first time since 2019, with Luton having enjoyed a spell in the Premier League since their previous meeting at this level.

Luton Town will be forced into at least one change following their weekend victory over Burton Albion after Jordan Clark was forced off with an injury in the 33rd minute, with the midfielder expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Daniel Gore.

Clark is set to join fellow injury absentees Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris in the treatment room, with the latter yet to feature at all this season.

Former Bristol City forward Nahki Wells marked his 15th league appearance of the campaign with his eighth and ninth goals of the season, scoring a brace against the Brewers last Saturday, and the Bermudian is expected to lead the line once again.

Having been in EFL Trophy action during the week, beating Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1, Ramsey is expected to make wholesale changes for Oxford's return to League One action.

Jamie Cumming started in goal for the midweek cup tie and could retain his place ahead of Simon Eastwood, who conceded three times last weekend, while changes are also expected throughout the defence, midfield and attack.

Gatlin O'Donkor came off the bench to score a dramatic winner five minutes into stoppage time against Wycombe and could therefore be rewarded with a starting place on Saturday, potentially at the expense of Tyler Goodrham.

Shea; Jones, Mengi, Andersen, Johnston; Walsh; Richards, Donley, Gore, Palmer; Wells

Cumming; Kioso, Long, Brown, Currie; Brannagan, Andrews; Missanga, O'Donkor, Emakhu; Harris

While Oxford United arrive at Kenilworth Road in high spirits, they face a side who have collected more points than any other team in the division across their last six league games, meaning the U's will know they face a difficult task to win at a ground where they have not tasted victory since 2017.

With that said, Oxford did manage to come away from their last visit to Luton with a point, albeit more than two years ago, and we expect them to repeat that feat, with the two in form sides playing out a 2-2 draw.

Following the news that Tomáš Souček has the opportunity to leave West Ham for a Premier League club in January, I have to say that I’m becoming extremely worried about the direction of the football club.

Claret & Hugh spoke to one of Souček’s representatives earlier today, and whilst they made it clear that his preference was to help fire West Ham back into the Premier League, it’s clear that he is a man in demand.

One Premier League club in particular is understood to be surprised that Souček has not been playing more frequently for West Ham and, as a result, is happy to test the water to discover whether he’s surplus to requirements at the London Stadium.

In my opinion, this is not something West Ham should consider, not for a moment.

Even before this news, I was going to put forward my case for Souček being involved from the start against Stoke City.

He’s consistently posed a threat off the bench, not least during last night’s defeat at Portsmouth, and has scored three goals as a substitute this season.

In the absence of any sort of goalscoring form from our strikers, Souček would seem like one of the most likely sources of goals in a team which has gone from being free-scoring and among the top goalscorers in the division to one that struggles to do anything other than hit the woodwork.

A lot has been made about West Ham having Premier League players, but I’m not sure how many of them truly are. Souček, however, very firmly falls into that category.

He’s a European trophy winner, an international player, a proven Premier League goalscorer and more than capable of scoring goals in the Championship.

This is a player who signed a new West Ham contract only last month and whose commitment to the football club has never really been in question.

But what has just become abundantly clear is that if we don’t use him, we’re likely to lose him.

And I find it highly unlikely that West Ham will be able to bring in a better player than Tomáš Souček in the January transfer window.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.
